This nostalgia galore. Battlezone revived for modern computer systems! This is a dream come true for fans of this classic.
If you played the old Battlezone from 1998, this will feel very familiar to you. The sights and sounds are practically the same, but the graphics are upgraded from the original release. There is little reason to not get the Red Odyessy as well.
If you haven't played Battlezone before, here is the basic premise:
In 1952, a metor shower rains down around the Bering Strait between Alaska and the USSR. The meteor remains, which are collected by the US and the Soviets, contain strange material that is named Bio-Metal. This material allows both superpowers to be able to make massive leaps in thier technology, far beyond even today's tech, although the general public is kept in the dark.
Fast forward to 1969, and the Apollo 11 mission lands on the moon, Basically the Space Race as we know it still happens as a cover. The real space race is what the story focuses on. Before Apollo happens, the US has already established a military presence on the moon, using very advanced technology and vehicles derrived from the Bio-Metal. In fact, during the first mission, you see one of the Lunar landers.
However, the USSR also lands military forces on the moon, called the Communist Cosmonaut Army (CCA) on the moon, and attack the US forces, which are called the National Space Defense Force (NSDF).   The story takes off from there, with missions taking place around the planets and moons of the solar system, not Earth though.  There is also a campaign where you play as one of the Soviets.
Additionally, the Red Odyessy DLC, back then called an expansion pack, takes place on Ganyemede, one of Jupiter's moons, with the NSDF fighting the People's Republic of China, which has also obtained Bio-metal from meteors. Their space forces are called the Chinese Red Army (CRA). The Chinese have there own unique units, and are not completely allied with the Soviets, reflecting the real life Sino-Soviet split. There is one campaign for each side in this DLC as well.
The game itself is a hybrid of real time strategy/tactics and first person vehicle combat.
You control your vehicle and it's weapons, taking part in combat, but also command friendly units, as well as building bases and collecting Bio-Metal (the only resource, which can be found scattered about the maps or can be taken from the wreckage of destroyed units).
Each side has a variety of vehicles, which you can change during a level. Hitting the 'H' key has you hop out of your vehicle and able to get in another one. You also eject automatically when your vehicle is destoryed. While outside the vehicle, you are basically an Astronaut infantryman with a plasma rifle. You are extremely vulnerable in this state.  So get in another vehicle ASAP.
Don't fool yourself, This is a challenging game. This is from a time when games were more challenging to complete.
If you are up for a challenge and want to try something different from more recent games, get this and enjoy yourselves!

I really want to like this game, I really do.
As others have said, it attempts to portray itself as a tactical RPG, but is little more than a computer based choose your own adventure.
Issues include:
-No way to customize your party members.
-Foes appear to not have the same AP restrictions as you do.  This enables them to move, shoot twice and kill one of your people, and then move another unit.
-Little difference between novice and elite members.
-Dozer abilities are too costly and appear to be one use / combat.
-Little reason to trust any group you encounter, so no reason to treat any encounter as anything other than flavor text.
-Foes jump onto the dozer and cut into it in about every encounter I've played so far.  What use is it to have an armed dozer if it can't be used to fight them off?
-Guns in combat can't be used above or below the set range.  This severely limits combat.  Combat is boiled down to a pseudo knight's dance to get your man to the right range to shoot.  Keep in mind that with 4 AP, this takes 3 of it (1 for movement, 2 for combat), leaving only 1 AP to move another.

When I first saw this game I fell in love with the artstyle I think it's a beautiful looking game and the style reminds me so much of Borderlands which is a series I'm very fond of. I also heard it was a roguelike which is a genre I've really been getting into lately. To my dismay when I looked at reviews for the game they were all very mixed. So I watched a few videos of the gameplay and the way you traversed the map reminded me of FTL and even the events have similarities at every node there are chances for a bunch of different things to happen be it combat or some kind of trader wanting to trade fuel for passengers. The combat looked pretty cool too I'm into turnbased squad games although this game definitely does take a unique approach with its point system so you can only do a few actions per turn for all of your characters so most of the time you're only moving around one or two of your squad. Needless to say I bought the game and I really enjoy it so far.
Pros:
-Beautiful artstyle
-Interactive devs*
-Interesting turn based combat system
-FTL style exploration
-Tons of replayability
*I know the devs are planning to add more content and that they've been taking everybody's complaints and criticisms into consideration. Initially I think they only had arcade mode, but they added tactical mode because it was what the players wanted don't hold me to that though I'm not positive.
Neutral:
-It's a very challenging game, which some will hate and some will love
Cons:
-Leveling system feels like it could be better maybe adding a perk system per level would help
-Range system is annoying at times I don't understand why snipers have the longest range but unless leveled have very limited hitboxes
Overall I definitely recommend this game if you are willing to keep an open mind about the combat system and you are into the roguelike-lite genre. I don't think this game deserves all the bad rep it gets and I'm looking forward to the new content.

I just can't bring myself to like this game. Despite my time in it and the fact that I'm forcing myself to finish, it is just an unholy slog to get through.
At the time of my writing this review, the "most helpful" reviews on display are 50% memes. That's not embellishment, five of the ten reviews are literally just jokes, four of those five are one sentence long. Steam's review system update is pretty trash in and of itself because of that (A surplus of actual reviews are lost because of early access spread, and yet you can make one that's literally less than twenty words and somehow that's a review)
Now to get into why I don't like the game ;
It feels bad to play, it stutters and hangs, at one point it crashed because I opened my phone when I got a research available popup in the middle of a dedsec phonecall. People are calling it optimized, but I've gone through every default setting from highest to lowest and I still have immense difficulty doing anything and it's not because of my rig (I have 430+ games on this account, a quarter of which are currently downloaded, and I can run all of them at their highest setting just fine despite how "unoptimized" they might be.)
The driving is awful. Seriously, vehicles feel like they have no weight, it's like the complete reverse of GTA 4's driving and threw out uncontrollably heavy cars for wheeled helium balloons. Not to mention the vehicles seem to all resist me driving them, and I thought my sudden veering to the left or right was because of another player hacking me since until I turned it off the game would start me in multiplayer matches WHILE I WAS PAUSED (I went cook dinner and came back, still on the ESC menu, to hear one of the dedsec crew warning me that Prime_Eight was siphoning my data, sure enough I close the "pause screen" in time to see a purple arrow on my minimap barreling towards me before I'm below another users stolen Billboard Truck)
The Car on Demand app is horrid, and personal vehicles matter less than the points on Whose Line Is It Anyway. I gave up on driving in the game unless it was a mission requirement just for the fact that it felt like the app was built to troll me. I was at a gas station 300m from my target? Send for my bike to be delivered. Can't find it? Check my map and see, oh, it's 600m in the OPPOSITE direction. Several hours into the game later I try calling for another vehicle from the app, only for it to spawn 250m away from me in restricted gang turf that you can't even drive out of. You needed to climb a fence just to get down to where my car was. Not that it matters because like I said, personal vehicles don't matter at all. Once you start or finish a mission, or get into a cutscene at any point in the mission, your vehicle is gone.
The game is.. nonsensical? I'm at a mission where someone very important to the story dies, and you go to a Tezca hideout to hack their server and find the people who killed them. Okay great. So I go in there and start shooting gangmembers, because this is a restricted area, and despite the fact it's the TEZCA hideout I'm suddenly informed I'm in conflict with the 580s and not the people who I was supposedly breaking into the base of.
The combat is awful, at least the guns. I have the Goodbye, World shotgun and and the DOT EXE Rifle. They do literally nothing to almost everyone. Not to mention the fact some enemies are literally invincible to gunfire unless you fire several rounds into their head. I went to a mission taking place on Alcatraz island, and found myself accosted by a fat white man who single handedly caused me to restart the mission about a dozen times. The problem I had with him? His blubber, like many "heavy" enemies bulletproof vests rendered all damage done to him by guns to be worthless unless I emptied two 30 bullet magazines into his face. Ubisoft does know that a bulletproof vest isn't actually bulletproof right? Let alone it doesn't confer that magical ability to every other limb on your body.
Overall a very disappointing game that fights me, as the player, at every turn (Literally, when driving is concerned)

I absolutely love this game. It is what the latest Simcity should have been. THeres only a few minor complaints mainly about highways, but most mods plus updates from the developers help fix them.

The game has a few fancy creative sides by letting you make arbitrary roads, but I don't think the strategy tag is valid for the product. As others stated, there is no challenge in the game, unless...
...unless you want to solve the bogus traffic behaviour of the game and making a big city with a decent flow of traffic - for no other reason than to please yourself.
I have seen people writing 25 pages long tutorials about how to overcome and workaround the odd traffic behavior of the game. I spent most of my hours on record (90%+) with planning the traffic of my cities. Which I would really love, but the fact that the driver AI is so terrible that it just blows my OCD:
I had 5 layers of superhighways overground, ground & underground just to manage the traffic of a town with 100.000 individuals...
There are so many problems related to the traffic AI, I just don't know where to start?
- Car drivers don't take actual circumstances into account in decision making
- It's nearly impossible to get traffic flow on/off the highway without seriously disturbing the ongoing traffic - despite the 3 lanes
- When a car is taking an exit from a highway, it will !always! change lane at the exact distance of that exit, its not just visually unpleasing, sometimes it will be totally impractical related to the actual road conditions
- Overcrowded streets solve traffic jams by making cars disappear - one of the most disappointing feature of the game
- Roads with more lanes don't give any performance boost as drivers don't make use of the extra lanes like how it would happen in real life scenarios (I've seen so many arguments about going very detailed in planning, but the facts are there, they just borderline use the extra lanes.)
- Roads with traffic lights are completely useless
- Trucks stop on the middle of the road for loading, stopping all traffic in the area
- Train stations get terribly overcrowded, unless you spam them everywhere - then the rails become overcrowded
- Pedestrians can cross superhighways while high speed traffic is going directly over them at full speed
- I can't really tell if it makes any difference to have terrible traffic or perfect traffic, the game just doesn't tell you how much that matters...
Other things:
- pricing of small and large versions of police, health care & fire dept are just ridiculous, it feels just random how they are balanced, police stations never build big, health care only build big if you want helicopters, fire dept always go for big - this sounds totally random isn't it?
- not enough content
- nice bus system, you can put the station on the road, but the manual management of the bus paths is just repetitive and boring as there is no point to it
- your buses quickly go overcrowded and are way to expensive to run & no bus ticket income
The game is unpolished, not much thinking behind. It just feels random. They didn't reinvent the simcity genre neither implemented the original in a better way. Sadly.
I would not recommend it above 5$.

At this point I would NOT recommend this game in its current state for even $5 let alone $18.
I won't say it's a dead game yet but it's starting to give me that impression with it's current rate of development or lack thereof.
(I.E. no major changes or fixes in almost 6 months)
EDIT 9/25/2017
TL:DR Hard crash and FPS issues fixed, But the fix introduced another bug that renders it nearly unplayable even for an alpha (I.E. load in, find food, reload when aproching said food) and the custom upgrade system (not sure what the proper name is) seames to have broken. the remaining issues I mentioned above either persist or I was unable to test. would like to be able to rebind keys but can wait for Beta release.
Overall feels like early alpha, has potintal as a dragon sim but has several gamebraking bugs that need to be fixed before Beta release. As of right now DO NOT buy if you want a polished/feature complete game, if you want to help find bugs, untill the reload issue is fixed it will be difficult to do.
The game still has issues, the devs have continued to work on it but several issues remain, the game no longer hard crashes and the FPS issue had been resolved with the reduced map size, now playing on the highest setting with no issue, but now has an issue of sending you back to the start position when you move about half way across the map cell after a loading screen. While I have not tested this beyond 30-45 mins of gameplay I suspect this is a issue with the transiton boundries of the cell not lining up correctly. This also presents and issue as most creatures are found on the other side of this boundry, rendering the first hunt quest unreasonably difficult to do. Flight controls still feel unnatural, this is mainly do to not being able to glide and results in a rather unrealistic/counterintuitive feel when using it. As for the map design itself, in that 30-45 mins I played, half of which I think I spent looking at a loading screen, I saw no noticable change the the terrain itself besides tree and Creature placement.

It's a scam. Are we really suppossed to believe that with all the funding that the early game excuse will pass at this point? The lack of communication is shady, we had to pay 15 dollars right off the bat without knowing what the end result was and you had the audacity after many hopeful people bought the thing to start a kickstarter for 30,000 dollars. You could have easily released a free test drive and worked on the game until it was finished, adding updates and listening to the community as you went along developing it, then when finished and start selling the final product based on how much you managed to get done and how many promised features you added. The thing crashes frequently, the interface is atrocious and a 10 year old could have designed a better interface. The save character feature that you say you implemented doesn't work. The programming is sloppy and the dragon model is ugly even with the 'new dragon models coming soon' thing that has been up in the corner as an advertisement for god knows how many months. It's infuriating how much of a scam this is and I want my damn money back. If this thing shows legitimate progress as a good game in the future I will buy it but my patience is finished and I am tired of the excuses.

So, I'm honestly not sure how quickly development has been happening on this game, but it's been around for a fair while, and it still seems like a pretty unplayable mess. Would not recommend at the current time. Will update when I can change that recommendation. Really hoping this isn't one of those alpha games that never turns into a product, because it's a neat premise.

Whether you are a US Astronaut piloting a Grizzly or a USSR Cosmonaut piloting a Golem, this is a review from when I started training up to the Mars missions.
Story: As an United States-based NSDF commander known only as Grizzly One, your assignment was to protect the Moon from the invasion of the Soviet-based CCA invasion, ultimately failing, but getting everyone evacuated in time. Now, you have to go to Mars to establish a base among the CCA already stationed there, until you find evidence of an ancient alien race and their ancient tech that could make or break space forever. As a time piece game, it's a "Cold War-gone-Hot" based game with some 1984-level cleansing to make sure the public never knows and, to be fair, it's one of the better games to execute the story. 9/10
Graphics: The graphics look pretty damn awesome. Playing it from a N64 version, the graphical advantage is apparent and it does do a lot of what it needs to do in order to be a redeluxe version of the 1998 classic. 9/10
Controls: To me, the tanks control like lubed up bananas on a wax floor like they participated in the Indy 500 (which does make sense considering they're hovering tanks), but the controls for ordering your troops or base around to any potential power source works well enough. 8/10
Music and Sound: Both are recycled from the original '98 version, but it would have been cool if the voice lines were updated with new voice actors, but add in the touches needed to make it sound like the originals. While I could just leave it at a 6.5/10 and get on with it, the fact that the music and a lot of the in-game sound can be replaced with mods is the reason I'll give it a 7.5/10.
Overall and mentions: As a person who has only seen footage of Battlezone 98 and had some trouble with Rise of the Black Dogs on the N64, I was disappointed to see how such a hyped game resulted in something relatively obscure. It's not exactly a diamond in the rough, but it is definitely something like a ruby in the rough. I hope that it does get more players, though most people will still decide to download the original 1998 game. 7.5/10 because it's not a bad game, but it does have some issues that could make it overlooked. However, I still would like to recommend it to people so they can try it out for themselves.

I played this game on an old Compaq Presario in the 1990's.  I then had the luxury of playing this patched and modified variant on a modern machine.  I have to say, it was a great improvement.  I played online and had a blast.  It was a fun beer night.  If you are looking at this title, you likely played it a long time ago, and if you liked it then, you will like it now.  People do jump in online from time to time, but be prepared to get stomped.
If you are new to the series, and somehow looking for old games, this title is great.  The graphics are upgraded slightly from what they were a long time ago.  The game is stable enough to run on modern machines and OS, and the multiplayer works.  The story is a cliche 1980's cold war saga, but with a twist that the USA and USSR are fighting a secret war in space.  What sets this game apart, however, is that it is one of the first games that combined first person shooter with base building and unit controlling RTS, AND did it relatively well.  There are a handful of games that had this style back then, but Battlezone 98 definitely ranks up there as one of the better ones.  You can jump in and out of your vehicles, build a base, build new vehicles, mine stuff, order battle groups around, or have them follow you, and pilot your way to glory.  There are plenty of vehicles to choose from, and the tech progression works up nicely.  A real classic Command and Conquer feel, with a first person 3d twist.  My only gripe is that this game isn't remade in Unreal or Unity 3d.  This game is a blast.

The setting, art, classes, enemy types etc. are all well done.  The problems come with the story and battle mechanics.  As many reviews have mentioned, none of the choices feel like they have any actual weight (and after many playthroughs I'm pretty sure they don't).  You accept the battles, you accept the new members, you say no to shady cloak-wearing dudes (most of the time).  It doesn't feel interesting and is not at all effected by your crew, dozer type, etc.
The biggest problem of all is combat, holy♥♥♥♥♥♥the combat.  I'm all for challenging, but c'mon.  Two moves worked in Banner Saga, why can't it work here?  Likely because you're being pulled in too many directions.  You need those resources?  Well then your team is going to lose a few members.  Want to kill off the enemy?  You might survive, but no resources for you.  And if you try to go for resources, you'll immediately be put on a clock in the form of the "Blitzometer."  In my opinion this should be done away with entirely.  This element essentially dissuades you from ever collecting resources unless you want to face horrible combat consequences down the road (which you cannot afford).  This, in turn, leads to eeked out victories that do nothing for you except perhaps a promotion.
With these seemingly minor issues the game turns into a chore, slogging through a series of "victories" only to realize you don't have enough resources, or gathering all you can and ending up with three team members.  I can understand balance, and I can understand sacrificing some things for other things, but these things arent choices, they're imperatives.  I like the setting of Bedlam, I just don't want to feel like I'm one of the poor fools in the steerage of the dozer.
EDIT:  As per the request of SkyshineJess, I'm updating the review following the "REDUX" update.  This is based on an arcade run on medium difficulty.  Overall, I like the changes quite a bit.
You can now pick from two different versions of the human dozer, with one team buff changing from the original dozer.  You can also pick 14 random crew or take less random crew in exchange for leveled up or elite crew, cool twist.
Blitzometer is still there but is bearable as I now only have to worry about spending energy cells on dozer weapons and team buffs.  This takes some of the edge off combat and gives me the opportunity to take some risks and go for resources.  Perhaps this is only in arcade but doing away with dozer upgrades was a great idea as it lets you focus on combat and resource collection much more.
Random encounters have definitely increased.  Some new encounters have been thrown in and the first 10+ stops of my arcade run were random enounters that benefitted me, might have just been luck though.  After those random encounters there were a few random battles and elite battles, all felt balanced and appropriately challenging vs. rewarding.  You can now take some risks and see the rewards, but if you take the risk and fail you're not completely screwed.  This makes combat, and the game overall, much more enjoyable.
Then cam the first boss battle.  At this point I had had so many random encounters that I only had 2-3 leveled crew.  And with this crew of semi-competent wasters I faced....Viscera, with 50 HP and 4 support (each at 10 health).  And to make matters way better the four support crew had my team surrounded.  Again, not sure if this is just terrible luck but the game went from balanced to janky in one move.
Overall, while I did get my♥♥♥♥♥handed to me by an early Viscera from out of nowhere, the game has improved significantly.  Combat is now more balanced, choices have increased, and the overall game is much more fun.  Kudos to the devs for interfacing with players and implementing these chances, for free.  The game is now easily recommendable.

Bedlam is definitely a game that fulfills its description - "Masochistically hard" describes it well. When you first load it up, beating the game feels like a pipe dream. It's not for everyone, but if you are a fan of Heroclix-style move-limited tactical games, give it a go.
PROS:
-Good writing.
-Excellent art direction.
-Moderate amount of depth - hardly Dorf Fortress, but you can plunge in face first and find some interesting bits.
CONS:
-Steep learning curve for combat.
-Unlocking anything is an exercise in luck.
-Frequent repeats of certain encounters.
Bottom line: 5.5/10. Above average, certainly not for everyone, but fun for those that like the genre.

The idea of simulating an esports player life draw my attention from the very beginning. And I can tell this game got me hooked for many hours.
Although it's in an Early Access stage, I think it's already in a good starting point to keep adding and improving content until the final release. To help the devs improve the game, I'd like to point out my impressions:
The base story is a compelling teenager story. I like the funny touches. This part is perfectly fine, but I'd add some extra sidequests - I know it's Early Access, but should be considered. For example, sidequests about pro players we look up to, missions to help their teams, help with friends problems. All this missions would be a nice way to move around the map, getting items, interacting with people while leveling up our skills. This way there'd be more variety of stuff to do and ways to level up, not just strictly twitching or playing.
The life simulator is ok, you have to manage your energy, stress and focus. It's easy to understand and work around it. However, the energy consumption needs some balancing, specially for some of the family relationship tasks (which drain a lot of energy).
The Steamy and Mirch minigames are fun to play with, but they're too simple. Since we have to play them many times to level up our skills, they should be more deep and challenging. They also could get harder over time, based on how good the player gets at them.
Now moving on to the heart of the game we find the team vs team matches, which simulate Moba and FPS. They are a team vs team fight simulation which use the members of the team stats, roles, strategies and skill cards. It's a bit difficult to get at first, but once you've learnt it, it's a smooth and challenging experience. However, I must point out that I'd like the match speed to be faster, since sometimes your opponent is so easy to beat that you just want to end his suffering asap xD
Runs perfectly on my pc and it's a nice looking game. Nothing bad to say here.
The background music is beautiful at first, but then gets repetitive when you've played some hours. Some more variety would be nice. Or lowering the background music...
During the matches, we can hear live casters giving the match a very realistic touch, although some sentences could have better acting.
20€ is a fair price considering the potential this game has. I've paid it happily, supporting indie devs can pay off (usually they make more creative games than AAA studios). Of course, I'm expecting the game to get improved... so devs, keep the good work going on!
I've seen devs reply in reviews as well as in the forums, so I think they're quite active and open to changes players may ask for. That's a great attitude and one of the reasons I don't mind supporting indie games :D
My overall feelings about the game are good and, as I've said, it has potential to be a great one. However, I expect the developers to put all their efforts to balance it, add more content, and improve what is already working well.

Thomas was alone is a game about teamwork and acceptance. Through its puzzle platforming, you meet many characters, including the titular character, Thomas (He doesn't stay alone for very long), Chris, and John. Though they are just squares and rectangles, most of them have some character, explained through a narrarator.
The main gameplay of Thomas was alone is, as I mentioned, puzzle platforming. To complete a level, you need to get each character into its respective box. This is where the puzzles come in. First you just need to deal with Thomas. That part is easy enough, just get the red rectangle into the rectangular box! Then Chris gets introduced. Chris is a cube, and can't jump as high as Thomas, so Thomas has to act as a stepping stool so Chris can get to the next platform. Chris isn't just a deadweight though, he can squeeze into small spaces and click switches. Each character has something special about them. John can jump super high, Claire can swim, and Laura is like a trampoline! Each character is unique in their own way, and that Aha! moment, when you figure out how to use each character's quirks to solve a puzzle is very satisfying.
Besides the gameplay, the story is pretty solid as well. The general gist of the plot is that all the quadrilaterals are AI's in a simulation. They weren't supposed to have two AI's in one simulation; as the game says: "That changed everything".
Each of the characters in the story has a very distinct personality. Thomas is happy and enjoys working as a team. Chris is grumpy but learns to accept his friends. John loves to perform in front of an audience and loves his ability to jump high. For a game about squares and retangles, there is a surprising amount of character development.
My highlight of Thomas was alone is in the chapter called "Design". This is where you play as all of the characters up until now. I really felt the strengths and weaknesses of each character, and how they helped each other.
My verdict on Thomas was alone is overwhelmingly positive. The visuals are great, the music is immersive, and all of the lines that the narrarator says are constantly adding to the character and "soul" of the game. I'd go as far as to call this game a masterpiece. 10/10

An interesting and incredibly artistic experiment that fails as a fun game to play. Unique and intriguing but ultimately not fun.
One part CYOA interactive fiction, one part resource management sim and one part token board game. Ultimately, it is fun to look at and interact with but entirely too random and without any way for the player to meaningfully affect things. It is far too easy to be set up to lose a generation and therefore need to start over simply by the initial tokens given, or by random events that arise through the course of play (particularly in the CYOA parts). Simply put, the game is too random and gives the player no real way of counteracting a bad roll of the dice with either skill or proper planning.
Given that it was supposed to be part of a series, which the author has since decided not to do, it is another mark against actually purchasing or playing it.

Please, forgive my bad English.
This vote has been one of my hardest decision here on Steam.
I was wondering while playing if this game should deserve a thumb up, but there were too many elements that keep me distant from the quick decision.
I've played the entire game with a gamepad and solo.
I started collecting all the possible rewards, but then I got bored and started to go straightforward.
I've also played a lot of platformer games, so I know a bit about them.
Graphics is superb, with fascinating animations, 3D effects, shaders etc.
Music is super awesome: they change constantly genre and get an amazing atmosphere although the strict change of setting in place.
Also, performance and the stability (even if I had 9/10 bugs during the playtime) of the game is a great point in favor.
The thumb up is due exclusively to this "bright side" of the game.
Now, this is an awesome title.
There is a big budget behind it, people that liked it (as it seems, a lot of people), and an unending list of people that worked on it.
It is evident how great has been the work behind this title, but still I didn't get why developers decided to develop some strangely annoying mechanics.
So, here are my impressions about the "dark side" of the game:
1) The game environment is unfair:
often, especially during the running part and when the scene dynamically changes its structure, there are a lot of unpredictable dangers that, considering the low field of view and the speed of the dangerous object, you haven't the time to avoid them.
This is the true motivation on why this game is a "frustration game": you must die several times to know the level and then trespass it (and that's why I started avoiding all the collectibles).
There are, also a lot often, enemies that don't act like they do normally but follow a pre-decided path, and often that path is unpredictable and hard to avoid when running or jumping.
2) That heart is mostly unuseful:
Do you remember when platformer's characters had lives?
Just to make an example, in Spyro and Crash there was the possibility to have 3 chances before dying.
The choice of giving to players just one chance before dying is not incorrect. It is nonsensical if the hitbox of the character reactivates after half a second, so you have no time to understand how to save the situation.
3) Hitboxes of the character, enemies and dangerous environment is not clever at all.
There are tentacles that hit you far under the bottom of the drawing and far under the upper; thunders that have a giant invisible hitbox; enemies that I still don't know how far to hit them.
Drawings are very pleasant to see but deceive you from their true collision box.
4) The controls and the physics are not good for a platformer game:
Maybe, here it'd be appropriate a "last but not least".
Now, I know that lots of people agree that controls are very good and movement are precise and the overall physics is cool.
I think here, maybe, is just a matter of opinion, but at least I want to give a reason to my opinion.
Movement is super smooth, even when not on ice, even when you are in the middle air, and this makes it very imprecise when jumping on platforms.
Running movement is ambiguous: you can start fast and get your movement even more slippery especially in the middle air when you have no more chances to strike a floating platform.
Jumping is decided by the time you press the button, but it has only two values, a high jump and a not-so-short jump, that does not give you the possibility to jump quickly between platforms while running.
When becoming tiny, all the physic changes and gives you a very hard time: lateral attacks are always charged, jumps are even more not precise and you are like constantly on ice.
Gliding with you hairs almost instantly cut down your speed to a constant value, that you can adjust but still with slippery controls. Also, you can't instantly reactivate the gliding, making the flying parts very painful.
Running on curved walls seemed a cool feature, but there are too many parts in wich you must jump to another wall and continue running. I never understood that system as more of half of the times the character started falling down or going backward (on upside-down running).
Without any doubt, this has been one of the most slippery platformers I've ever played since years and those 4 points are why the game should have deserved a bad vote.
Anyway, the work with graphics, music, humor and cuteness saves this game.

TL:DR: Story heavy with quirky game mechanics and a whimsical plot.  A bit of over-stereotyping the "gamer" archetype, but remains fun for the most part.  Mini-games could be a bit more polished, and loading screens are excessive to the point of immersion breaking.  Worth picking up, but perhaps wait until the game drops in price.
First Impression Video:
The game begins very story heavy with a bit up of setup before the actual "game" starts.  This is fine, but be forewarned.  You follow the part of a typical high school student trying to become an esports pro.  Before you see the title screen, you are required to choose a real life professional esport team.  I'm assuming that these are teams the game developer was able to get licensing for.
Portrayal of the gamer archetype is fair typical; with your mom not being accepting, bullying at school, a mentality that better gamer gear equals better skill, etc.
At the beginning you have two main genres to specialize in: MOBAs and FPS's.  Training in both categories is basically the same activity, where you are given a certain length of time to click all the red opposing team players without clicking on your blue teammates.  A very simple system, but will become quite repetitive over time.  This stresses your character out for some reason, and talking to other people relieves this stress.  That seems a bit backward to me, but okay.
Overall, actions you take throughout the day are dictated by the amount of energy you have.  Chores, school, and gaming all take up energy.  Sleeping and food restore energy.  You can make friendships, flirt with girls, and watch other players on the in game Twitch clone.
My feelings on this game are mixed.  Not sure it portrays the image of professional gamers in the right light, but it does seem to make an entertaining game.  A bit out of context for the majority of serious gamers who have been out of school for several years.  Also, the loading screens are excessive.  Immersion breaking at the frequency they appear.
While I do recommend this game, I feel that it would be a better fit in the $10-$15 range, so perhaps wait for a steam sale.

Normally, I write reviews after I am done with a game. However, I don’t think I will retire or complete this game in the near future and I believe it deserves more attention, I just write down some thoughts now. May edit later.
At first glance, Castaway Paradise resembles the famous Animal Crossing game a lot. They indeed have several things in common, but CP has its selling point too, like farming and its unique square art-style.
Good:
+ A lot of furniture and outfits to get/change. I mean a lot of. XD
+ Free DLCs and festival updates. These introduce new contents, including items, island decoration and more, in the game and are often time-limited. I myself is busily farming gems to buy all the Thanksgiving items now.
+ Various ways to make the profit. You can farm seeds, grow trees, catch fish, water flowers, sell stocks or help out the island dwellers. By doing so, you are well paid back.
+ Daily challenges: This is by far my favorite part. Completing daily challenges to get the new dress, gems, and even new bandages. Why not? And even better, bandages can be displayed in the mysterious room now! I’ve always been curious what function that room will serve.
+ Easy control. I play Animal Crossing on 3DSLL and also tried CP on the phone. But Steam version is far easy to control. I usually use both keyboard and mouse.
+ Colorful art-style which makes me really happy.
+ Welcoming community and responsible devs.
+ No microtransactions or social media accounts needed.
What I think will be better if added/modified: (Some of these features are beloved ones in Animal Crossing)
- Multiplayer. It will be much better if we can visit our friends’ islands.
- Larger fish/shell/bug variety. Seasonal fish or bugs.
- Ability to decorate more houses. Like town house and other dwellers’ houses.
- More dwellers.
- Use the boat to travel to another island.
- I want to be the mayor! XD
In sum, this game is fantastic, especially for casual gamers! If you are into cute and colorful things or if you have some minutes to spare or if you like farming/decorating/dressing, give this game a try. It will amaze you.

After a violent storm you find yourself washed up on a tropical island and are quickly welcomed by the other inhabitants, from there you're free to do as you wish be it farming, completing quests, gathering collectibles or simply decorating your new home.
Castaway Paradise is a sandbox simulator reminiscent of games like Animal Crossing with quite alot to do, tons of objects and colourful graphics: it's a good game if you like the genre despite its slightly annoying controls and UI.
-charming, colourful graphics and art style
-tons of different quests, since they're randomized you'll never run out of them
-a plethora of outfits, objects and decor to buy and use
-three different collectible categories (bugs, fishes and shells) plus badges for completing daily quests
-there's lots to do, buildings to reconstruct after the storm, an upgradeable house for yourself, stock market, farming, gates to unlock new areas etc..
-once you get things going it's easy to gather enough currency to get what you want
-good length, you'll need about 12 to 15 hours to unlock every area and rebuild everything
-finicky controls, it's sometimes hard to position yourself near the tile you want to interact with
-the UI feels awkward while you navigate tab after tab to find what you want to buy or use, the auto-select for things you can bury/ plant/ tools to use can also get in the way (e.g. when surrounded by several interactive elements, when it forgets what seeds you are planting thus making you buy the wrong one or when it insists at presenting collectibles before seeds when you're near a planting hole). It works overall, but it's annoying
-villagers are forgettable overall, as are their dialogues
Castaway Paradise works well as a sandbox thanks to the huge amount of content it throws your way, you're simply free to do as you wish whether it's fishing, farming, hunting for bugs to donate to the museum or decorating your house: the random quests are generally easy enough and provide a steady income for you to invest on the island, a few ones (like catching a certain fish or farming one of the crops with long timers) can be a bit dull but can always be skipped with currency.
It's charming graphics and light-hearted take on the genre also makes the game perfect for a younger audience especially considering its gameplay is easy to learn and open to letting you be as creative as you want with how you put objects, flowers and trees in the various areas.
All things considered Castaway Paradise is a good purchase if you like the genre especially considering there's not many games like this one around on PC: it'll provide a good amount of content to keep you-and any family members- busy.

Call of Duty: Black Ops 3 is the 12th CoD game to ever be released and 4th (after World at War in 2008, Black Ops 1 in 2010 & Black Ops 2 in 2012) of the 3arc cycle released in November 2015. Since it's the game developed by treyarch, Black Ops 3 is seperated into 3 different game modes - Campaign, Zombies & Multiplayer.
Campaign is starting off rather cruelly - in the first mission you lose all of your limbs fighting a much stronger robots which straight into the year 2065 full of cybernetic abilities and upgrades. You and your team fight off some bad gays like always, get betrayed as always and win with some sacrifices in the end (as always).
Multiplayer is as any usual multiplayer before, set all in maps in 2065, having to choose from up to 10 classes, each having different ability. These abilities are all class-specific (except for Blackjack), you level up as usual, sometimes get dropped cryptokeys, of which when you have enough, you can open supply drops in the Blackmarket which can drop you a certain camos and skins to customize your characters. It can also drop you a very rare (Legendary) weapons themselves, which are the ones you will want ;p
Zombies is as always mostly targeted for coop gameplay but solo is not restricted. There are 6 maps (with all DLCs so far up to 23.5.2017 on PC).
- Shadows of Evil - it's set at the same time as Mob of the Dead from Black Ops 2 with futuristic weapons and first apperance of a new weapon - Apothicon Servant, a tactical - Lil' Arnies (same as monkey bombs but squid-ish) and boss called Margwa - it has three heads, only one opens at the time and you have 3-5 secs to shoot it, only after you kill its all 3 heads, the boss is going to die, there is also a secret bug with Civil protector but I won't spoil it too much.
- The Giant - it's a remake of Der Riese from World at War and Black Ops 1 having futuristic weapons only with the return of Wunderwaffe DG-2 and hellhound rounds.
- Der Eisendrache - it's a map situated in a castle set high in the mountains, returning hellhound rounds and Panzer Soldat - boss which first appeared in Origins in Black Ops 2. As in Origins, here you have 4 elemental weapons but this time they are Bows - Storm, Wolf, Void and Fire. They have their own strengths and weaknesses as staffs from Origins but over-all Storm and Wolf are the best. And also first appearance of a new special weapon ragnarok DG-4.
- Zetsubou No Shima - it's a map situated on a stand-alone island near Japan with the first appearance of Spiders. they have their own special round as hellhounds and also like on The Giant, they spawn during the rounds 20+. here is also a first apperance of few specific guns but most importantly a weapon called KT-4 and a special weapon Skull which can make instakill zombies or temporary make zombies ignore you.
- Gorod krovi - it's a map situated in destroyed Stalingrad by war & dragons (YUP, DRAGONS!) in Russia with an appearance of old-school guns like MG-42 or PPSH. And a first appearance of a weapon called Ray Gun Mark 3.
- Revelations - it's map situated after a one bad guy destroy the worlds and splits the Eearth into tiny islands, most of the islands which are avaible to play on are remakes of older maps (for example: Shangri-La, Nacht Der Untoten or Verruckt) with a return of old weapon Thundergun.
ALL OF THE ZOMBIE MAPS have some background to them, some easter eggs which joins them together and other maps and have a nice experience to play on. I'm a high round player so I can tell you that getting here 100+ on any map is much easier than before.

This has a pretty fun concept.  This is a side scrolling puzzle game where you take control of puzzle pieces in place of your usual platforming characters and you must move these pieces to designated placed around the levels.  You will have multiple pieces within each level to choose from and you can switch which piece you are controlling at will.  Each piece must be touching its exit to complete the level.  There is no real "death" mechanic or punishment for failure, so this can be played pretty casually.  Some of the puzzles had a little challenge, but nothing I would consider difficult or frustrating.  Overall it was very enjoyable.  It's not a very long game, so you might want to consider that with whatever the current price point is if interested in this game.

Dragon: The Game has been in development for 2 years, with a team of people working on it, and all that is offered is something that cannot even be called a demo. I refunded this game almost a year ago after quickly realizing the path it was taking, and following it to this very day, I can see I made the RIGHT choice on refunding it.
A year ago the public build for this game were abysmal. No sounds, crashing everywhere, no multiplayer, NPCs falling from the sky, caves filled with holes, very unresponsive and basic melee attack, etc. Now from what I've seen, (and from the most recent update) sounds have been added, there is much more diversity in the NPCs, crashing seems to still occur for some people, etc. While the game HAS improved somewhat, you have to realize that over the duration of a year, this team has added things I've seen other devs that weren't even properly funded do within 4-6 months. This game has been funded successfully for 35k on Kickstarter.
I look toward the devs of Yogadventures and then I look back at this game, and I see a similar fate. Yogadventures is infamously known for being funded, but handled by inexperienced developers who simply gave up in the end, and plopped the filth they had been working on for about a year or two on their kickstarter supporters. And EVEN then they seemed to have made more progress then this game has.
I'm not saying this dev team would do such a thing, but for HOW LONG they've been working on this successfully funded project; and what they have to offer within the duration of 2 years, I simply don't think people should purchase this game. Atleast, not until we ACTUALLY see some real progress here.
Don't get me wrong here, I WANT this game to be what it promises. We ALL WANT a Dragon Sim. I really hope the devs will be able to somehow pull this off. If you are a DIEHARD fan of dragons, and have always wanted a game like this, get it. If your like me and are a bit skeptical on the duration of this game's development and progress, wait either for a price drop or, again, when we see some real progress. Best of luck guys! :)

Where do we begin...
Battlezone 98 was a game far ahead of its time.  When first person shooters and strategy games were still in larval stages while platformers and other genres dominated the market, this game brilliantly blended the two bold new genres together in a format unlike any other.  Not only did you build buildings and commanded armies, you went on the frontlines with them with powerful tanks, and if you were feeling lucky, you can disembark one for REAL sniper skill challenges as a humble trooper.  They have a wonderful mix of both units, and arsenals that can shake the game up faster than a bartender on crack mixing a martini.
The primary drawbacks i site on this is the lack of open ended skirmish both offline and online, if they did this like other strategy games did back in the day this game would be perfect, and resources are very finite making gameplay restrictive.  The game is very challenging but can be a real controller/mouse to the screen difficult, and not in the challenging way that uber gamers desire, more like, "WHY THE ♥♥♥♥!? HOW!?" where you can only have a margin in the lower single digits of error to proceed.
The game had immense potential, and it still does, but as long as the gameplay remains this restrictive it won't go further than it is.  Despite the flaws, i still recommend this hidden gem to anyone seeking a witches brew of intense first person shooting combat and calculating real time strategy gameplay molded into one. Когда ты говоришь BBT, то обычно мало кто понимает о чём ты, пока собственно он в этот BBT не поиграет.
BattleBlock Theater стал той игрой, в которую ты можешь затащить любого человека с любыми игровыми вкусами. Это платформер, который придётся по душ любому, т.к. он прост в освоении и прохождение. Тут наверное заиграет что то внутри хардокрищиков, говорящие из глубин их мозга: "Да как вообще можно создавать платформер в котором ты не будешь постоянно умирать?". А вот так вот. Первое: В BBT ты постоянно умираешь. Постояяно. Второе: нужен хардкор - всё просто: включи режим "Хардкор".
Как уже говорилось выше, игрушка представляет из себя ненапряжный платформер, с полным, кооператвным прохождением. Стоит отметить что 1 игру пройти реально, но это  не доставить столько удовольствия, поскольку игра сильно ориентирована на кооперативное прохождение и для этого созданы все условия (и ачивки). Нужно кинуть друга на другой берег? -Делай подсадку. Не нужно кидать друга на другой берег? -Делай подсадку. Нужно достать золотой клубок на другой части карты? -Делай подсадку. Хочешь потерять друга? -...(думаю сами поняли).
В игре так же есть какое - никакое ПвП в виде арен или соревновательных мини - игр, но про них я расписывать не буду, т.к. никогда не пробовал. Игра полностью поддерживает workshop что не может не радовать. Прошёл всю игру? Пройди ещё несколько десятков тысяч уровней, созданных пользователями! (Кстати ещё один плюсик в копилку хардкорщиков. От хардкорщиков, для хардкорщиков). Редактор уровней прост до невозможности - это развязывает руки многим пользователям.
В игре присутствуют класные фичи по типу кастомизации и оружия. Кастомизация тут ограничивается выбором типа головы и её формы. Хоть это и единственный способ украсить персонажа (Здесь я опустил выбор цвета игрока), но его вполне хватает, учитывая что тут несколько сотен этих голов, которые надо ещё и открыть, а играете вы в конце концов в платформер, а не в sims (тут могла быть шутка про кастомизацию современных MMORPG, но её не будет). Следующий пункт - оружие. Его тут около 20 видов. Оно нужно для того что бы изничтожать (какое хорошее слово) котов. Либо что бы  помогать себе и товарищу проходить уровень. Или же что бы мешать. Или же что бы мешать товарищу проходить, изничтожая котов. Либо же что бы изничтожать товарищей, попутно мешая котам проходить вас. И т.п. (ну вы поняли)
Структура уровней тут везде одинаковая: На карте расположен выход, который открывается когда вы соберёте 3 гема (гема, потому что огранённый изумруд - длинное словосочитание). Всего на карте от 6 до 7 этих гемов (редко - 5). Собирать их или нет - на ваше усмотрение. Так же на уровне всегда присутствует 1 золотой клубок. Обычно он запрятан в каком - нибудь труднодоступном месте. Зачем собственно всё это нужно? Ну во первых за прохождение уровня вы получаете оценку по пятибальной шкале от A до F. Так же есть A++ но что бы выбить эту оценку нужно умудриться собрать всё на уровне, да ещё и уложиться во время, которые тут в принципе не ограничено кроме финальных уровней глав (об это чуть позже). За гемы можно покупать головы - по 10 за шт. При чём голова даётся рандомно. Вы выбираете только её форму (Шар, куб, цилиндр, пирамида). После 10 купленных голов одной формы цена возрастает до 15 за шт. Золоты клубки тратятся на покуупку новых оружий, по 5 клубков за шт. К слову все виды оружий открыть куда проще, чем все головы.
Теперь немного о прохождении самой игры. Игра делится на 8 глав. После прождения каждой главы вам открывается доступ е следующей, и рассказывается часть сюжета (Да, это платформер с сюжетом). В каждой главе 9 основных, 2 финальных и 3 дополнительных уровня. По поводу основных уровней всё описано выше. Финальные уровни, схожи с обычными, но у вас всегда есть ограничение по времени, по истичению которого вы проваливаете прохождение уровня. Дополнительные уровни устроены по принципу финальных, но для того что бы открыть следующую главу проходить их необязательно.
Отдельно стоит отметить саундтреки к игре. ЭТО ШЕДЕВР! Я никогда не слышал ничего более подходящего для платформера, чем данные произведения искусства. Не буду больше ничего говорить, это просто надо слышать.
Игра очень часто светится на распродажах по 69 р., хотя свою полную стоимость игра окупает.
Вроде всё сказал, не думаю что многие прочли до конца, но спасибо за внимание!

I first played Rayman Origins on the PlayStation 3, and it quickly won me over with its colorful and fun atmosphere, creative platforming, and above all, THINGS TO COLLECT!
Rayman Origins is a collect-a-thon 2D platformer, giving you multiple things to collect:
The collection in Rayman Origins is incredibly fun and rewarding, with constant indicators of how complete you are with your collection, most notably on your save file. I just can't play this game without getting everything!
Of course, who would want to collect anything if there wasn't any fun platforming involved? Rayman Origins is one of the most creative platformers I've ever played, with multiple power-ups, underwater levels where you can actually swim, levels that involve you flying on the back of a mosquito, running on walls, flying up sandstorms, the list goes on. Everything in the game is fun to go through and puts a smile on my face, which brings me to the graphics.
Rayman Origins was the first game created with Ubisoft's own UbiArt engine, and my, is it gorgeous! Everything in the game is completely hand-drawn: Rayman, his friends, enemies, and especially environments. One of the reasons I bought this game again on Steam was just so I could sit close to my monitor and admire the backgrounds that much more! Everything in the game is happy and colorful, and being sad while playing this game is simply impossible.
The music is also fantastic; as fun and creative as the game it's in, and complements the levels beautifully.
One warning about this game, however: it does get frustratingly difficult later on. Thankfully, Rayman and his friends have infinite lives, so you can retry levels until you beat them! (or ragequit. Whichever comes first.)
Speaking of Rayman and his friends, one of the best parts of this game's experience is its local co-op. Grab 3 friends and you can embark on the entire game together, collecting Lums (and yes, there is a bit of competition involved in seeing who collects more Lums xD) and struggling through precise platforming while one of your friends keeps messing everyone up. It's loads of fun and the way I first experienced the game!
Finally, Rayman Origins is a gem and a platformer that is not to be missed. Even $10 is a steal for what I honestly believe to be one of the best games ever created, so buy it now!
--Ian PK

Good tactics seem to be beaten by the sheer luck of the computer who seeming has the upper hand in every battle, playing on normal unlocks nothing. Skirmishes slowly wittle you down, men and women from your crew dying frequently and your resource pool tends to be pityful. Yet as desperate as it all seems and as frustrating as it can be, I really enjoyed it. The graphics are great, the character models cool (especially the elite units) and the gameplay fairly satisfying. I don't think this has the same charm as FTL (another rogue-like I'm a big fan of) but you might find yourself investing a fair amount of time into it. Where FTL is hard it feels fair or justifably unfair (if your ships unprepared), this game is random and as stated earlier the A.I. is really lucky (at least it seems it). The route your taking is guess work at best. When trying to avoid a faction which I hate due to its abillty to disapear I had to enter it's area to progress. My whole crew including my best men were wiped out really early on therefore making it very difficult to comlete the game. Prehaps I am being slightly wimpish and forgetting the rogue-like priciples. I bought this game months after it came out so didn't encounter some of the bugs people did upon release. I also bought it in the sale so I am very happy with my purchase, therefore I whould recommend it despite some, probably, minor complaints. It will fill my post-apocalypse void until the next Mad Max film is released or I get bored of Fallout.

Don't be afraid of the 'mixed' warning symbol, the negative reviews this game got early on was largely due to the real weird design decision that led to combat sucking mad hardcore. v2.5 fixed that with the 'tactics' mode so the game, while still real hard, is no longer grueling.
Then 3.0 came out. The revamped version has a ton of new content and combat is even better thanks to it adopting a more x-com style.

The art is nice but there is very little of it and it gets reused a lot. It is way too expensive just for a bunch of artworks.
The characters you recruit all have a badass biography but they actually have the same stats as the lower ennemy mooks.
The first time a character levels it gets a significant boost in all its stats (dmg/health/range/mvt) and gets a full heal (btw the new costume is crap). The next levels only increases your dmg by 1 each time. You don't get to choose which stat to upgrade. There is no perks or skill tree.
The level system is completely broken since the only stat that change is dmg and there is no level/stat cap.
A soldier starts with 5 dmg and can level to 100 dmg if you grind enough. The consequence is that you can 1 or 2 shoot bosses. It is even more ridiculous with sniper units that stay at very low health: they can one shoot anything but any random mook can one shot them.
You can recruit elites. Elites tend to have more health and more limited movement but any over-leveled unit you have will deal considerably more damage.
You can unlock extra dozers but they don't get unique abilities or weapons. Their screens use the same art as the starting dozer even if the current dozer is a giant mutant creature. The APC unit is the same for all dozers. The starting crew of a faction dozer is not fully staffed with unit from this faction.
The enemies are basically all the same but with a different skin and a lame ability on top. Mutants should rarely use guns but instead use mutant abilities (acid spit, spikes, tentacles/extensible tongue, etc.). Some factions should have pets (war dogs for marauders, mutant beasts for mutants). Factions should differ in numbers, abilities, stats and technological level
The combat is crap but could be easily improved:
-allows 4 ap by turn with a limit of 2 ap by unit
-introduce special abilities (the gunslinger can throw grenades for instance)
-introduce special attacks: charged/spread shot - a minigunner may be able to hit multiple targets at once. This is one of the biggest issue with combat: you have to slowly take out ennemies one by one and you can have 10+ at the same time.
-implement a real cover system
-give the unit the ability to carry items in battle
-have not all the battles be with a ton of low level mook but have battles with less enemies but more veteran/elite enemies.
-have more weapons on the dozer but with a tiered system (the more powerful a weapon the more it costs in energy, has a longer cool-down, may actually require a specific ressource such as individual nukes)
-have unit movement & range makes sense
-weapons & powers may cost less but have cool downs & the amount of energy may be capped
-have new classes (the rocket cyborg shouldn't be treated as a sniper) & hybrid classes
The combat is bad but what is much worse is the complete lack of content and replayability: you will get the same events over and over with the same outcome. Also there is too much points of interest their number should dwindle the more you explore a location.  Interesting point of interest that require a specific item  should stay on the map so that you can revisit them later when you find the item. Of course there is also way too many battles. It gets old extremely fast.
The game is also lacing events such as mechanical problems, freak climatic events, conflicts inside the dozer, etc.
There is no choices & consequences. The game is missing towns where you can trade resources & recruit dudes.
Some mechanisms do not make any sense:
-Why do 300 passengers flee after a lost or abandoned battle ? They will die in the wasteland.
-Why can I recruit passengers from warring factions ? It will bring war to the dozer.
-Why the marauder dozer can recruit cyborgs their sworn ennemies and vice-versa ?
-Why does the mutant dozer consume crude ?
-Why can I sell my passengers to slavers or merchants to get ressources ?

The game was tagged as an RPG in the store when I bought it, so that was a disappointment.  The tag isn't there now.  For what is now being advertised, I think that the game plays well enough.  Keep in mind that it IS NOT an RPG at all.
With the last few patches, battles are more enjoyable.
While the game looks like an in depth Mad Max style RPG/CTS almalgamation, it's not.  It's a chess game with a resource management minigame and a map encounter minigame.
Your soldiers are underpowered for being understaffed.  You get only a max of 4 to use each battle.  One dies?  That sucks buttocks.  Better hope that doesn't happen too often.  Maybe you'll get another one through a random encounter.  Maybe your soldiers will die too much because you are facing 12 enemies in a battle, and you just got pwned in 5 battles just like that.  And while you are trying to maneuver your soldiers so that the enemy can't either double team one of your soldiers and kill them in one turn or have an opportunity to first: walk up and then secondly: horribly murder your soldiers, you are also expected to gather resource pick ups on the battlefield to ensure your "dozer" vehicle can continue the trip to the mythical Aztec City.  Maybe you try to use an equalizer in the battle, only to realize they aren't that effective and cost way too many power cells to make their use practical because power cells are a precious resource, and you already used all of yours up last battle.  It's challenging.
You get 2 actions per soldiers per turn.  So does the enemy.  Some points of interest have a silhouette with a question mark, where you will have to face 3 to 5 baddies and an elite.  The elite will one hit kill your soldiers most of the time.  If you win, then the elite will join you.  You will probably lose 3 of your soldiers killing them.  Do we call that a victory?  Draw maybe?
And if you manage to pull off the journey, which you probably won't, you unlock another vehicle with worse stats and 1 more equalizer with which you are expected to try again.
I tried the new version and found the gameplay much more enjoyable. There is NO character development, NO equipment, NO merchants to sell said equipment, and NO level up management. It doesn't look like the game I thought I saw in the trailer or an RPG when it was tagged as an RPG at the time of purchase.  Be aware of what the game is, if you buy it.

The developers seem willing to listen to review feedback from players, which is a good thing because they will end up making more money if they do.  A lot of independent game development companies don't care about reviews and will even ban people for negative feedback, which only results in their being blacklisted among prospective customers.  The willingness of the developers to change and expand their product is a refreshing positive change for an indie game company, and I'm looking forward to seeing how this game changes over time.

Only a few vestiges of the original mobile iteration remain, but they're pretty glaring -- energy timers on most actions and a progressive level cap on the shop catelogue.  You'll be actively hampered by the former until level 15 and can't complete the latter until level 34.  The PC version may not have cash IAPs, but still uses mobile tactics to gate content.
The handful of NPCs populating the island are such helpless simpletons, they actually amplify the feeling of being marooned on an island Tom Hanks style, except you're surrounded by sock puppets instead of volleyballs.  Without
crafting system, farming and fishing become a repetitive grind for EXP and currency.
On the positive side, the devs are fairly responsive and post in the community hub regularly.  I don't know how many more (if any) player suggestions they plan on incorporating since leaving Early Access.  They do roll out seasonal/event updates and limited edition item sets, but the majority of LE sets are holiday-based and only appear once a year.
Underneath the grind,
boils down to a reductive decoration-sim.  It lacks the depth & breadth of genre heavy-hitters like Farmville or Harvest Moon.  I bought this on sale for 50% off from the Humble Store (so no refunds).  I really wanted to find more depth in this game, but even with so much time sunk, I
can't strongly recommend it in one direction or the other.  Perhaps it's better that there's no neutral option, because I'd say ambivalence is damning enough.

Yes, it is a board game. Many negative reviews here seem to be holding this game's mechanics against it, but the simplicity and chance are the point. Watching your dynasty morph and rise and fall depending on the drop of a coin or the unexpected outcome of a cyoa choice is what makes it such a joy.
This game manages to create the feeling of passing through an enormous and tumultuous swathe of history with grace and simplicity thanks to the well-designed mechanics and some well placed, but not overwrought, pieces of flavor text. The writing isn't showy, and there isn't too much of it, but it is just the right amount to keep this epic story of a family's progress through the generations feeling vivid. The slot-machine mechanic may seem strange at first, but it models feeling of being desperate for food with too many children, or feeling driven to climb the social ladder to avoid being crushed beneath the wheel of history, incredibly well.
Basically, this is like Crusader Kings II except you roleplay the peasants. CK2 gives you a map of the world and armies to place throughout. 7 Grand Steps gives you a coin and a wheel. You provide the luck and determination.

When it's on, a more organised group can use each other as stepping stones, or a chaotic mob will push each other off ledges. Tethering forces you to work with a partner. Anyone can create maps in the map editor, which are automatically downloaded from a server before each match like many Source games, but quicker because the game is small.
Anyone and everyone should give it a go

I really enjoyed playing through this game. The platforming was fun and simple, a variety of characters with a variety of abilities keeping the stages interesting. None of the levels ever felt too difficult or unfair.  My only downside with the platforming was the tedious nature of moving a character that does not jump high. This was annoying especially over large stretches of high platforms, where I had to repeatedly create staircases with my larger rectangles to get my smaller rectangle to the goal point.
What really sold the game to me  were the unique personalities given to each rectangle. Each character really felt like an individual, sold by the wonderful narration and fun character traits. I felt like I found something to identify with each character. I would recommend this platformer to anyone looking for a few hours of engaging entertainment and wanting to get emotional over rectangles.
