Okay so befor I say anything, Major... MAJOR props to the devs. They've come a VERY long way from their restart and have worked closley with the community and taken all their feedback to make this game great.
Okay, now to the actual game. It takes place in a post-nuclear world where your objective is to get your passangers across the wasteland from the only safe city known to the planet called Byzantine to a mysterious and legendary floating palace that is the only true safe haven called Azctec City. You use a veichal called a Dozer to traverse the wastelands which comes equipped with different weapons and battlefield upgrades.
Traversing the Wasteland: You have X amount of Food, Crude (Fuel), Power Cells, and Passangers. Food and Crude are consumed daily, when you travel from one place to another x amount of food and crude is consumed for x amount of days it takes to get there. You can use power cells to upgrade your dozer or use it's weapons on the battlefield. Upgrades consist of Reduced Food and Crude consumption, Reduced amount if time it takes for combative crew members to heal, or reduce the amount of power cells it takes to use dozer weapons. Upon starting a game you may chose which faction you want your crew to be.
Factions: Humans, Rouge AI, Mutants, Marauders, and Cyborgs.
Humans: Well.... They're kinda average. Nothing special about them. At all. (As far as I can tell)
Mutants: Every time their cobmative turn comes up they regain one HP.
Cyborgs: Every turn they lose one HP but gain one Damage (This ability will not kill them, when they reach low enough health they will no longer gain damage and will not lose health)
Rouge AI: Every few Turns they become invulnerable to damage
Mauraders: Every few turns they gain the ability to move a few extra spaces.
The Crew: This consists of all the four classes and ranks of crew members.
While selecting your Dozer and Faction, you also get to choose from four crew setups.
No Leader, No Elites, No Veterans, 12 Rookies.
No leader, 0 Elites, 3 Vets, 8 Rooks. Leader, 0 Elites, 1 Vet, 7 Rookies.
Or Leader, One Elite, No vets and 5 Rookies.
Leaders are a unit specific to the dozer but some can also be found as a weakend version of itself as an Elite. Leaders are very powerful. Elites can be found in the wastelands and are also powerful, Rookies are your average crew members that, if they achieve three kills become a veteran.
The four classes consist of Gunslingers, Deadeyes, Trenchers and Frontliners.
Gunslingers: Dual pistols, medium agility, medium damage, High Health. If hit from a target within their firing pattern they return fire.
Trenchers: Shotguns, High agility, Higher damage, Medium Health and has knockback. If next to their target they ignore the benefit of cover.
Frontliners: Highest agility, Lowest damage, Most agile. Considered to be the tanks of the crew and they only attack with Meele, Baton and shield. Always ignores cover.
Deadeye: Lowest agility, Highest damage, Lowest health. Can inflict immense damage and if lucky achieves an instant kill headshot. Snipers of the crew, but very fragile.
This isn't like XCom where you can attack in a certain range, each class has a shooting PATTERN, it's hard to explain you're better off looking up gameplay and looking for the red dots as people move and shoot. After successfully completing a combative encounter you gain resources immedietly. If you lose, you either lost all your deployed crew (4 people) or fled. Upon losing passangers leave the dozer.
There are two modes, Tactics mode and Arcade mode. In tactics mode each squad member gets two turns, if they fire upon their second turn their attack only does 60% damage. (Please note, later in the game the enemy has MORE units then you do and WILL overwhelm you if you do not make use of your dozer weapons. Upgrade earlier, so you don't need to be afraid of using your powercells later.) I'll be honest, I don't play much of Arcade mode so I won't ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t you about it. I can't help you there, I'll come back and edit this section later.
To win you must traverse the wasteland and find four artifacts, then fight the supreme ruler of the Wastelands, King Viscera. While traveling to find these artifacts you may come across resources, but more importantly Points of Interest. POIs can be anything, from simply a fight, to stumbling upon a new recruit, all the way to finding new battle upgrades and weapons for the dozer. Also equally as important are Elites. Elites as mentioned befor are powerfull units that can put up a real fight. To achieve these units, you must find them marked on the map and defeat them in combat. This will go a long way in helping you get to Aztec city.
SO I would definetly recommend this game and I must give huge props to the devs for sticking with this game for oh so very long and making it great, working closely with the communits. I'll summarise quickly at the end here but please read the whole thing. <3
Pros:
- Beautiful Artwork/Graphics
- Clear path to goals via tutorials.
- You feel accomplished after finishing a run and unlocking the next dozer.
- Combat is quick to get used to and easy to learn
- Character designes for Elites and Humans are pretty cool.
Cons:
- Traversal system is just a little bit unclear... At times you'll want to get to somewhere on the map, but the problem being is you can't see movment options past either what is immedietly available or what has already been traveresed, so sometimes you'll be RIGHT NEXT TO your destination, but you can't go to it and have to go to three other places first without knowing how many places you'll need to travel or which path to chose (major waste of resources) but it's usually dealable and dosn't get too bad.
- The combative system in this game IS NOT for everyone. Some people will despise the way in which classes are set up to be able to shoot in a pattern instead of a range. Example: Your dual pistoled gun slingers become stupid and can't bring themselves to shoot someont standing right infront of them because they have to be X amount of tiles away, in a certain tile pattern away from the gunslinger. (This is for all classes, in different patterns.)
- Crew designes for factions other then humans get dull. All the Females have one portrait and all the Males have one. The Humans are the only ones with diversity. And they don't have an ability (as far as I can tell).
And that pretty much sums it up! After reading this you should look up some videos befor buying it to really be sure if this game is for you. It's a good game now, a really good game. But it is not for everyone. At all. HUGE props to the devs though! Go check out their other games, give em some support. ^^

Skyshine's BEDLAM is an interesting concept for a game to say the least. The Tactical RPG Strategy Roguelike combination is a brilliant blend and mixture of different genres, with the inclusion of an Invigorating Mad-Max word filled with rich lore and an unforgivingly psychopathic landscape truely makes the game feel grand and enjoyable. The Simplicity of the game and with the addition of the brilliant tactical battle system I kept on finding myself returning to the relentless Bedlam again and again.
However, after a while, It does start to feel ever so slightly tedious as there really only are only a couple events and each one having more or less the same exact outcome.  Added with the fact theres not really much to do in terms of exploration. I really want to explore the lore and the people of Bedlam and I feel there should be more aspects in terms of exploration and things to do in the Game. Maybe having NPC towns that are owned by a non-hostile faction that randomly dot the map a different time each gamemode. In the town you have the abillity to buy and sell supplies, maybe even buy and sell crew members and even do quests for extra rewards and goodies.
Thats my only real complaint of the game in general. However the game itself is still brilliant. The great artstyle and music really does give the game its overall charm and atmosphere. All in all the producers did a cracking great job at this game which hits the Tactica Stratlegy Roguelike combination straight on the head.
In my opinion, its worth the full £15 (or $20 for my American Buddies)

FTL mechanics in a Fallout Tactics universe. Still got the odd kink to solve (e.g. targeting area isn't draw correctly after firing).
The battle mechanics are painful. You have to collect resources mid battle, units have a set range (e.g. snipers can hit only 4 tiles away), no overwatch, cover is given even when flanking the enemy.
Wait for a later release before buying.

Great concept with poor execution, Skyshine's Bedlam could be good but definitely feels like it needed a proper Early Access period.
With shallow exploration, poor resource management, a lack of real choice in event decisions, no dozer customization, little difference between unlocked dozers and no real interactivity between the world and your crew, there isn't much reason to play through more than a few times. The lack of anything interesting makes combat the main-focus, which is a love or hate affair; a poor example of games like FTL.
Currently, the game is an un-advertised Early Access title. Previous updates show a lack of direction on the developer's part with respect to the future  for their game, as they continue to experiment with features that should have been nailed down before an official release.
If you're interested, wait for a sale. Although combat is controversial, there are many other issues that make the title disappointing.

After the developers released the REDUX update to this game, I gave it another whirl and I am glad I did.  Below are a few points that I thought were improved:
Combat system
Oh man, this is so much better than the last time I played.  Each character on the battlefield gets 2 actions per turn now instead of a shared pool of actions. I love the premise of Rocksmith. Ubisoft’s execution of the game is a pretty shaky though.
The basic tutorials are pretty entertaining. I was surprised to find the announcer has some good tips [for easier tasks] and will point out to you when you’re on the wrong string/fret. The ‘guitarcade’ games are a clever way of getting you better at the basics. They sadly don’t scale to your skill level/performance so they can get pretty repetitive if you’re having trouble improving.
Menus are sloppy, inconsistent and all have a little sliding animation that needs to be finished before you can move on. Getting the game to recognize you guitar is also a nightmare. Not impossible, just frustrating.
The accessibility of using a microphone is great but is lacking in the accuracy department. I purchased a pick-up for my acoustic and had to use a USB ADC to amplify the signal enough to get Rocksmith to work at all. I understand that really quick fourier analysis can be tricky, but the game is designed like there won’t be any muddle or delay.
In the end, nothing feels worse than knowing for certain you’ve played the right chord/note just to have the game ignore you. When the game gets confused you can lose a streak or even all your progress in arcade. In lessons, the inablility to pick up some techniques makes the announcer bombard you with tips. Lessons expect perfection [before the practice song] andwill forcibly slow you down when you miss a note a few times. The mental backlash of, “But I am doing it right”, is oh so frustrating. As for noobie, the incompletable harder lessons aren’t necessary [yet], but the fact that I can’t even give them my best shot is a disappointment.
Unlocking more of the catalog requires completing a selection of mini-objectives, some of which feel locked away behind the functionality of the game.
I’m not convinced that buying one of their magic ‘Real Tone Cable’ would improve my experience as I had a friend who had an electric guitar and the cable have a similarly convoluted and inconsistent time putting everything together.
Below, I’d say, 20-30% of a song learned, things seem to ramp up fairly. The game only adds in small chords when you’ve done that same small 5 note bit flawlessly several times. Beyond this region, however, that game gets way tougher, going from a few notes between strings to a barrage of several large and unfamiliar chords.
There are some good setting in the practice mode you can enable mid-song. I just wish there was a sight read mode that would stop and let you catch each note before advancing to avoid just giving up when the game throws giant chords or high fret notes at you.
If you’re looking to play more songs than the ones in the base game, Ubisoft has provided quite a few extra songs via steam, at a premium. It’s great that they’ve got a large selection that lets you expand your library towards artist you enjoy but $3 per song [1.79 on sale] is asking a little too much in my opinion. Lucky, to mitigate this probably, the unofficial modding community for Rocksmith is remarkable. They’ve got a ton of recognizable tunes from all sorts of famous musicians that Ubisoft didn’t get around to monetizing. On the downside, most don’t have the game’s variable difficulty/learning curve, so, for beginners, mods are more of a distraction.
If you know how to play the instrument, I’d totally recommend the game. I think it’d be a pretty entertaining way to some extra practice in. If you’re interested in guitar, and have one laying around, this isn’t a bad place to start. By which I mean, the game should work more as a supplementary way to practice than the only thing you do. Rocksmith isn’t perfect and there’s a lot to be gained from looking around for more resources/tips or even committing to lessons if you feel you need more specialized help improving. Learning sheet music can also drastically increase your potential repertoire.
Whether or not Rocksmith will become your main source of experience with guitar, it’s still a great idea with a lot of potential, just know that it’s not as fantastically as if advertises itself to be.
Games that teach you are always something to be admired. There’s not much of a demand for instrument learning games, as licensing costs pretty high, but imagine if there were higher quality games for all sort of instruments…

Castaway Paradise is sold as an RPG, but really, the only RPG element I see in it is the questing. I would compare it more closely with a social game or even a mobile game than any actual RPG. There’s no enemies, and no story beyond “You’ve washed up on the shore of this island and now you can help the people rebuild and make it your own home”.
The menu is lacking in the same way mobile and social games are, there’s no sliders for volume, just mute or unmute things, no windowed mode options, though alt+enter provides you a window the exact same size your resolution.
Starting the game, the music was decent, but repetitive. What sound effects there are are also rather typical of the kind of game. I also wasn’t completely sold on the graphical aspect of the characters, which is an undecidedly blocky 3D version of animals/humans, but I did like the aspect of the island/items/everything that wasn’t characters and clothes. The clothes designs were cute, but I still didn’t like the characters shape, which really ruined the looks of the otherwise cute designs.
On Castaway Paradise you can take quests from the villagers, farm crops, catch fish and bugs, shake trees, plant trees and flowers, cut trees, pick up weeds and trash to clean up the place, dust off cobwebs, upgrade buildings a couple times and decorate the island and your home, and then some I probably forget. There’s also a bank that will allow you to earn some extra money for using it, as well as a mini stocks market that’s not really too difficult to use at all. You can also unlock new spots to visit on the island, which isn’t overly large to begin with.
It’s all rather nice, and I appreciate that it has something more to do than just plant crops or just do quests, but it doesn’t feel terribly fulfilling until you start decorating the island and your house.
The crops and things you plant have a timer on them, as with all social games, which means you can’t play when ‘you’ want but have to wait around until the game decides the crops are ready.
Some of the tools have a ‘stamina’ meter, a certain amount of times you can use it per x time, that refills overtime. This goes away when you reach level 15 and become “VIP”, which was their way of removing the need for micro transactions. This also unlocks more shop items, cheaper items (“discount”) in the shop, etc.
The game does have something kind of addictive to it, and I did enjoy my playthrough, which is why I recommend it, but despite it, it ends up being boring and, at the risk of sounding redundant, repetitive. Why? Well...
Starting by the fact that the quests are all the same: plant x of this, pick y of that, take this to z, talk to w; rinse and repeat as there’s only so many characters. The rewards they give (xp, sometimes items and pieces to unlock new areas of the island, and gems/money) are not really worth the time. The money you make from them sometimes ends up being more than what you need for the quest - for instance: Decorate the island, where you have to place two chairs that are worth three times as much as the reward. Granted, you can pick up and resell if you only want to finish the quest, but you only get part of the money back.
The quests can also not be cancelled, at least not that I’ve seen, thus you’re stuck with either gathering enough money to buy the things they want you to get so you can finish the quest (or waiting however many hours for crops when you want to play NOW), or gathering enough money to pay off to “fast finish” the quest, which is also kind of expensive. Since you can’t really preview and accept or reject the quests, and since you can only have 3 going at a time, it gets really boring.
Planting and selling crops also doesn’t shield much money when you take into account some of the crops take 11+ real time hours to be ready… on stage 1. Some have more than 1 stage, though you can choose to pick them while they’re smaller rather than let them grow to its fullest.
Meanwhile, upgrading the buildings and purchasing things is quite pricey in comparison. It’s not impossible, but it’s kind of annoying. In the long term, it almost seems more worth it to stand by the stocks and wait for them than wait for crops and do quests, and neither turns out being overly fun after the first few rounds. Even catching bugs or fishing, which are the most interesting aspect, get tiresome.
There is a little annoying ‘bug’ that if I try for my character to go somewhere else while it’s running an animation, it will get “stuck” in that direction and when it stops doing the animation it will walk the way he was looking instead of the way I’m telling it to, but it’s hardly game breaking. I do, however, wish you could stack things to do (so do this, then water crops, then come over here kind of thing).
On the upside, the game has some free DLCs that add a bit of (shop) content, and they also run events. They have leaderboards for the collectables/bugs/fish you catch, and it is kind of a cute game, all things considered, but it is the kind of game you go onto for an hour or two and then get tired with.
Recommended: Yes, if you like social games and don’t mind it being terribly repetitive after the first few quests (which I guess you don’t, if you like social games ;) )

Rayman Origins is just as the name suggests, a return to the origins of the franchise, which started as a 2D platformer, and also brings back a few of the earliest designs and concepts used in the first Rayman game.
I fell in love with Rayman after playing Rayman 2: The Great Escape, and after that, Rayman 3: Hoodlum Havoc.
I never actually played the original Rayman more than the first level, i did not enjoy it, i am not a 2D platformer person.
But since this year marks Rayman's 20th birthday, i decided to play this game, and wanted to actually finish it, which i did.
The game is very enjoyable, even for someone who doesn't really plays 2D platforming games, i can even call it very fun.
It has lots of levels, with different themes, and different playstyle to many of the levels, like running levels, where you must be as fast as possible to reach an enemy/cage/etc, there are shooting levels, where you fly on a mosquito that shoots, plain old classic platforming levels, as well as boss fights, which you must avoid the boss' attacks, and then hit him in a weak spot.
The engine could use some polishing, but it works just fine, except some parts where you might get stuck on a ledge or stuck inside an enemy, but these are pretty rare and not noticable.
The level design is very well done, and requires skill and thought, where you cant just sprint and jump through the obstacles and enemys, and it contains lots of funny and very creative themes to them.
As you progress through the game, you gain abilities like flying, shrinking and diving, and you always end up using one or the other after unlocking them, so kudos to Ubisoft for not forgetting that they implement some features and forgetting to actually make you use them.
the game took me about 10 hours; its not very long but its definately worth its 10 dollar price tag.
I recommend the game to any platforming fan, and ofcourse, Rayman fan, but dont expect anything like the 3D games.
In conclusion, i really like the game, its fun, its intuitive in the current market, and its Rayman, meaning it contains lots of humor and an interesting storyline (although kinda confusing at times).
Its not the Rayman i wanted, but its still very fun.
P.S. it also contains a local co-op options, but since i'm lonely, i couldn't really try it, so i didn't write about it, but i bet it would be lots of fun.

A strategy based board style game which I found strangely addictive for around 10 hours game play before it started to get rather repetative. The suggested playtime of ~15 hours was about right for my completed game.
As many other reviewers have noted this is a difficult game to describe. I tried to write up a detailed description of the game but is was messy and made little sense :(
The best I can say is that is like a board game where you are awarded tokens which you use to move around the "board" by matching the pictures on the tokens to the pictures on the "squares". Beads appear on the squares and you are awarded points for landing on squares with beads on. You accumulate points to progress in the game.
The board is actually circular and you only see about a third  of it at a time, each turn involving the board rotating at least one "square". The board is made up of up to 3 separate "rings" and depending on your tokens and how you have progressed you can move between the different rings.
You can only move clockwise by matching pictures but you can choose to move anti-clockwise by moving to the next square occupied by another character. Note that you generally have to keep moving clockwise to avoid being eaten by crocodiles which happens when you drop too anti-clockwise on the board.
There is a background story generated as you play the game as you can marry, by landing on the same square as another character who is also available for marriage, have children, by landing on the same square as your partner (who you also control). Eventually your characters will die and you will need to nominate an heir at which point the board is redrawn.
The game progresses through distinct phases called ages & a new age brings on a new board layout and the background story options change.
The game is saved on exit, although note there is no cloud save!
There is textual help which is fairly helpful although personally I found out how to play the game mainly by trial and error.
5) Must have - stop whatever you're playing now and play this
4) Worth the asking price and considering as your next purchase
2) Only purchase if it is heavily discounted

I remember playing this game back in 98, it was the first ever PC game I remember playing. So having said that I preface with nostalgia having a factor here. The game looks pretty good for it's age, and unlike other games I have, playing on my 65" tv isn't haveing any effect on the games frames.
Pros:
A very interesting story
Interesting units and tactics to play them
Two sepereate campaigns with provide their own challenges
Good blend of FPS tank fights, with a healthy blend of RTS you can't forget about
Simple and direct inputs mean you can just a few buttons quickly and get tasks done
Looks great (for being originally from 98), and still plays pretty well
Back in the day, the multiplayer was pretty fun, but it's been awhile since I played that
Cons:
Sometimes the AI is dumb as a sack of potatoes...
...When they aren't being dumb, they kick your♥♥♥♥♥
In game doesn't really tell you nearly ANYTHING you need to know about how to play other than move and shoot, so expect to go to outside sources to learn how to do more complex manuevers, commands, and tactics.
Unit limits - you can have 10 units from three categories (offense, defense, utility) so it's not quite a massive strat game as some others.
Expect your units to have no self preservation skills, and they don't always like being called back to retreat either.
So if the cons seemed a bit heavy, its because I want to be honest in this review. If you like RTS games, and like what you see it is worth it. The way the game feels even today is smooth and just like I recall from nearly two decades ago, whereas normally nostalgia games don't live up to their memory this one most certainly does indeed. Coming back to it as an adult I wonder how I ever played this as a kid, and where it's been all my adult life.

From the 20+ hours I've played as off 2/12/16 or the 12/2/16 for you Americans, I can safely say this game is really good.
Story and Missions: Straight from the start you get a very strong intro in my opinion and throughout the course of the 20+ hours the side missions all have a story to them that are either explained in detail or extremely briefly, which is still good seeing that in most open world games you just get the side mission, you do it, then you're done and the repetitive crap over and over again. Straight from the start as well and throughout to where I am, I am still flooded with missions and side content to do it's insane. The main story is really good. All of them so far have been really enjoyable missions where you usually have to break into somewhere. e.g. Nudle (Google Pisstake), !NVITE and HAUM which is a business that takes advantage of the peoples trust in them to sell data. About halfway through the story something happens to a character I personally got really attachted too over the course of the 20+ hours. This involved a gang called the Tezca's, and when I started off this game I wanted to not kill anyone because I didn't think it was in Marcus' nature, but after this I got into a Tezca hideout and just ♥♥♥♥ing killed them all because of this. After that, the gang members in the area heard the shots and about 15 guys flooded me, cops ended up showing up and it was just a complete ♥♥♥♥♥how, but this shows how a simple thing like this can really make you want to get revenge, which brings me onto the next part.
Characters: For me, especially Wrench and Marcus are extremely well written and well voice acted, this is the first game I've played in a long time, if at all that actually feels like you are listening to real people talking! Props to Ubi for the voice acting and script, ♥♥♥♥ing brilliant. Sometimes the dialogue does feel a bit cringey but I think thats happened on about 2 occasions, one involving cornholes?
Gameplay & Animations: First off, the parkour is ♥♥♥♥ing great. The animations feel smooth and flow extremely well. I find it really fun to just to get on top of a random cop car and get them to chase after me just for an exciting cop chase. The stealth feels great but there are some issues, the AI when you get detected and kill them a split second too late, everyones on you, most of the time they don't even say anything but everyone magically knows. Overall, using the RC and Drone to your advantage feels really good and using the stun gun and gunplay feels good, as well as the 8-ball on a rope thing feels really statisfying to hit people with.
Controls: Driving, wow. For me it even rivals GTA 5's driving, it feels really good, especially handbrake turning around a corner, it gives you that statisfying drift and you do feel like a real race car driver. Sometimes with the cover system it can feel a bit dodgy but it isn't a big deal at least to me. The running feels really smooth.
World: San Francisco is a vibrant, expansive map which includes Oakland and Marin which all are extremely detailed and colorful. With ScoutX which I will explain later, it just feels like an alive world full with plenty of landmarks.
Extra things: I love the fact that Ubisoft have implemented the song system so you can listen to music of your choice while roaming around the world. ScoutX is a system that makes you explore San Francisco and see all of it's Landmarks. Songsneak is a really nice feature as well as it feels like an extra collection. The phone which is your main interface in the game feels like a real phone which is really important to me.
Multiplayer: I've tried a bit of this with the bounty hunt missions which are extremely fun, the invasions which to me are a bit bland, would of liked maybe something more with it. But what really stands out is the multiplayer co-op missions. There are a wealth of these and I'm not joking. I have literally done about 20 - 30 of these and every time I finish one it seems like more and more keep popping up. I understand it can get boring after a while but if you and your mate love to do co-op missions together you will love this.
Ubisoft, well ♥♥♥♥ing done. I can safely say this is one of the best games I've ever played, to me it even matches Witcher 3 in terms of detail, story and fun. Please keep making games like this.

At this point, I can't recommend this as an early access title. It's probably one of the three crowdfunded titles I actually regret purchasing. In the last two years, very little has changed in the actual product. While there might be "under the hood" work being done, there is also very little communication from the developer despite numerous requests for information.
The last round of customer complaints on lack of updates elicited a post from the developer where he stated "I can communicate more regularly and authentically."
This was on July 10th.
It's now nearly two months later, and not a single post or bit of information has come from the developers. It could be a deserted project sitting in early access for all I know, but there is no communication present.
Even before this, it was spotty - this started on steam EA and had a number of purchasers (I'd guess a few thousand). Then, after that initial open-up for purchase, there were a few updates, almost no communication from the devs, and then silence for several months afterward. Things became active again for a month with a Kickstarter which got another 50K to develop the game, a couple of updates during that time and then complete radio silence for 2-3 months. Until the people that purchased their game practically shook the cages asking what the hell was going on, can we hear anything at all about this project?
When tracked down and found in a livestream, the developer stated they were afraid to communicate because of possible "misunderstandings".
This is a pretty bad excuse.
No one misunderstood anything, no one was being negative in their forums, just asking "can we get an update?" or "has this project been abandoned? I haven't seen any sort of communication."
Bottom line, I urge you with all caution NOT to purchase this early-access title. Due to the lack of communication from the developers, the strange excuses, and the lack of overall progress over the period of two years, this is most likely not going to be finished, and any money or hopes put on this are likely to be a wasted effort. I do expect another round of crowd-funding before they finally go totally dark and abandon it, but the pattern has been pretty clear since this project started.
If the behavior actually changes, then I'll be happy to update the review. At this point, though, buyer beware. They don't have enough personnel or resources in order to make the project they are selling.

Since I've recently hit my 100 hour mark, I thought now would be a nice time to give my thoughts on the game.
My experience with Rocksmith is very great so far, as I tend to try and put in as much time as I can whenever I decide to play. I ended up downloading hundreds of songs from customforge, a website with free downloadable songs to play with Rocksmith, along with community forums about the game. This is much nicer than buying official DLC, but it's still good to buy DLC, as Official Downloadable content isn't available on that website.
I, for the most part, started learning guitar solely by using Rocksmith as my primary tool. This game is more a tool than a game. The main learning I use this game for is "Learn A Song", where you literally just get to learn whatever song is in your Rocksmith library. Since I've downloaded my songs from Customforge, I have spent most of my time here. I have put minutes into "Session Mode", although I've heard it is a really nice way to learn scales and other useful things here. You also have "Lessons", which is a very great tip-center. It can teach you the simplest things, like strapping your guitar up, to holding your pick, to other things. It also has more advanced lessons, like tremolo picking, to teaching you chords. Again, I rarely use Lesson mode, and instead I just end up winging it. "Guitarcade" is one of the most useful items here. It provides you with multiple games to play, all with your guitar. They teach you how to pick from one string to another, to getting you used to switch from this chord to that chord, and even teaching you how to quickly pick strings. There are other things you can do, but these are the ones you'd probably end up playing the most out of this game.
For the most part, yes. Obviously, you need to put the time in to see results. I seriously don't recommend only using this game to learn. YouTube some songs and how to play, or simply Google search the tabs to a song and try that way. Play outside of the game sometimes, take your guitar on vacation with you. Play as much as possible. I also recommend using customforge for custom DLC songs. You have access to so many songs to play you almost won't ever even think about buying Rocksmith's official DLC.
Overall I love Rocksmith and what it does. This is the best way to learn guitar, if you don't have someone else to teach you. If you are debating between this and Yousician, definitely get this. It may be a little pricier, but Rocksmith actually works, unlike Yousician.
11/10

Castaway Paradise is a game that offers Farmville / Animal Crossing style gameplay with beautiful visuals. There are many quests and activities to do, such as farming, fishing, building, catching bugs, and more. Your ultimate goals are to repair the bridges connecting all three of the large islands, repair all of the buildings on the islands, and complete the quests given to you by the NPCs. The only downsides are that there are a few bugs, some quests can be a bit boring, and some tasks have too long of a wait time.

[TL;DR at the bottom]
So I have not played much of this as of yet, but this was a rare occassion when I played. Let me explain. You see, I'm the type that gets bored with things quickly. It's hard to keep my attention, so I'll play games 1 hour at a time, usually. But this game? I thought I had been playing for 2 hours, had been playing for 4 hours.
But anyhow. I'll be doing this review with things I deem as pros and cons, you may not like some of my pros and may like some of the cons. There will also be 'Ehs' which are ~. These things have pros, but cons too.
Pros:
+For starters, the artstyle is just.. MWAH! Is sublime ladies and gentlemen, you can see it from the screenshots. It's just perfect for a game like this.
+Collecitbles! Again, perfect for a game like this, especially when you can put 'em into your house! Speaking of which...
+Your house isn't started off being a big house. It has 3 tiers. You start off with a tent that has a smallish room and you can see the rooms you can unlock. You spend gems (the currency) to upgrade your house to a house. Then once you become a VIP (which I haven't gotten to yet) it can become a mansion.
+Fairly big map
+Varied NPCs
+Great game to play in short bursts
+Amazing timekiller
+Great soundtrack and SFX, they perfectly compliment the artstyle.
+Nice amount of outfit customization and furniture.
+Ability to decorate the island how you like is pretty damn cool.
+Fishing and bug collecting is done well I feel.
+The leveling and XP system is cool, makes alot of things feel rewarding and worth doing.
+Daily 'log-in' rewards. Gives you a reason to keep coming back everyday, always like that.
Cons:
-A bit too grindy. It takes quite a while to get gems and most things cost quite a bit. I personally like grinding, but it's a tad too much as it is.
-Parts of the map are locked off, but if you asked me, it feels like too much of it is and it takes too long to get to. You see, you have to collect 'Puzzle pieces' to get to other areas in the map. To get to those areas you need 9 of these puzzle pieces which you can get from certain quests (which aren't too common) and by paying 2500 gems. But as I said, gems aren't easy to grind so again - a bit too grindy.
-As with all games, I say the same thing, it's always a con if it doesn't have character creation unless there's a set character story.
-There are 'waiting periods' where you have to wait for actions to go through, like waiting for a tree to grow fully or a building to upgrade. It makes sense, but I personally think there should be some way around it, like paying gems to speed it up.
-From what I've seen so far (if someone can confirm/deny this it'd be appreciated) there seems to be no night/day cycle. Always day and also no seasons.
Ehs:
~'Stamina' So you have tools to use in order to do things. Axe to chop trees, watering can to grow plants and saplings, pickaxe to remove rocks, etc. But they have uses, for an example - the pickaxe. By default, the axe has 5 'Stamina points' as I'll call them, which are essentially 'uses' It takes two uses/Stamina points to remove one rock. You can 'refill' your points once you've used them all by using gems, but it tends to be expensive. They regenerate overtime, but I feel it takes a bit too long.
~Farming. Now farming is actually a fun thing to do on the side and works well with the waiting periods, BUT I feel like the rewards from doing it make it not worth it. I don't feel like it pays off enough.
~The UI. I dunno, just don't know how I feel about it, it's just.. 'Eh'
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Human Fall Flat is a physics puzzle game which is really special and hillarioudly fun to play.
In single player, it's a fun adventure, getting froma area to area, exploring new scenery and finding ways to solve the puzzles facing you.
In multiplayer, it's that but a WHOLE lot more. Maybe you'd take the *friendly helper* role and help your friends up when they can't quite reach the big rock you're standing on or hold down a button so they can cross a chasm. Or perhaps you'd take the *lovable prankster* role and surround your afk friends with rocks or toss them off cliffs for a laugh. There's just so many ways to mess with each other but also have fun and solve each puzzle together.
And last but not least, controls. I find that the keyboard controls are very easy to use, and that was an important thing for me as I have difficulty playing games with bad or wonky controls.

If you like Animal Crossing, you will like this game, however...
Animal Crossing would technically be the one I would be more likely to pick up after playing this game. That's not to say this game is bad, far from it! However, this game seems more suited to be a Facebook or Tablet game than a Steam game.
You play as a boy or girl character who has washed up on an island inhabited by Animals. You are given a tent, and told to live life on the island. Similar to most openings of Animal Crossing. The gameplay involves your character performing tasks around the island on a Stamina based timer. Now, this isn't a bad thing, as it makes you feel the need to come back later and do more tasks, however, the Questing system which usually involves you doing these same tasks, is VERY repetitive. You will be given a task like: Farm 3 items, or Collect X Items. This let's the game down in my view, as this really doesn't offer much variety.
Tasks you can perform can range from Fishing to Farming. Fishing, Bug Catching and Farming are your 'Money makers', but don't expect to roll in the cash instantly. Farming is on a timer, similar to Farmville or similar Farming Apps. Fishing and Bug Catching relies on the game spawning  random insect on the island for you to catch. Same for Fishing. Fruit can be grown on trees, which again, is on Timers. You can donate Bugs, Fish and now Shells to the Museum (Once the bridge is built and you pay to rebuild the Museum) for fun, much like AC. You can rebuild Villager homes, but... This really served no purpose in my views. Some quests you are given seem to cost MORE to complete, yet, you can pay to skip the quest with your game currency and save thousands on the costs of items you had to buy. Overall, the game gets very repetitve and becomes boring, but again, this is only an opinion. Would I recommend this game? Yes. This game does have it's qualities and can be fun to return to daily, but until more content is added, there is very little to do once you have experienced everything. 7/10

Even if the game is still in constant evolution (bug fixes and addons), so far it's already a great, fun life sim.
It feels a lot like My Sims and Harvest Moon mainly, where you live in a determined scenery rather than a randomly generated one, with its set of characters instead of alternating villagers. Also, you have an experience meter that levels up by solving quests given by the characters or doing simple chores like pulling weeds, breaking rocks, planting flowers, trees or vegetable seeds; the more you level up the more you unlock goods and even other parts of the island. But there's also plenty of Animal Crossing "touches" there, like anthro animal villagers, several themed clothing pieces and furnitures or a wide selection of bugs and fish to catch and sell, donate to a museum or use any other way you like.
But of course, the game has its own identity. The mouse + keyboard control is practical and works wonderfully. The game is filled with great humor, with lots of popular culture allusions too. One of the strongest points is the indoors and outdoors cutomizing freedom: the majority of the items and collectibles there are not limited for use only in a certain place. Too bad you can't interact with them (so far, maybe).
Bottomline, a worthy title for life sim or just casual gamers.

Okay first of all anyone that flat out hates this game because it's a port or loves it because it's Berserk is short sighted and needs to see the big picture, this isn't a good game but being a port has nothing to do with that. The biggest issue I have with this game is how they try  to cut so many corners that it completely ruins the experience, you literally cannot enjoy this game like you would a regular hack and slash because it's a Berserk game and it's so clear what it's missing. Here's a list of all the short cuts they took and how it affects the game.
-Use the movies to substitute for cutscenes, this wouldn't be so bad if they were at least consistent and didn't butcher what they lifted from the movie, they apparently got the rights to use the movies but couldn't let the full scenes play out so that it was a coherrent plot?
-Butchered the story, they not only remove things from the plot but also rearrange and oversimplify the story, almost all nuance is lost, they continuously try and hit at it which you will recognize if you are a fan of Berserk but it will remain unsatisfactory
-They flooded the levels with meaningless which just don't work with the narrative causing continuity errors and fundemental issues. If you're going to flood the game with meaningless nobodies then make them die in one dramatic slash, don't make me sit there slashing multiple times to clear nobodies
-Enemies are incredibly minimal with an abundance of unnamed ones, basically you've got the scrubs, the base leaders, the commanders, and then the unique named enemies, the amount of scrub enemies could be cut by 90% and nothing of value would be lost
-The difficult and combat are beyond broken and emberrassing, you can basically walk through the battlefield unempeded when it's filled with scrubs, that is unless you set it to Berserk difficulty in which the very first mission which has the lowest enate difficulty will become near impossible because scrubs literally litter the battlefield and will now lunge at you instead of just standing around and whenever they land a hit a significant amount of healt is removed, this wouldn't be an issue, it is expected after all that a higher difficulty mode will deal more damage but they connect so easily and they're so many of them it's like if you went out into a field of grass and for every blade of grass you touched someone shot you with a 9mm, kinda makes it hard, doesn't it?
-Even on the lower difficulty playing against apostles, the one thing that should be the most fun, is near migrane inducing because anytime they hit you you'll be stunned but even your heavy attacks don't stun them, the game tells you to use support weapons but even then the throwing knives don't help, and the repeating crossbow does about as much damage as a real life paintball gun, the only weapon that's affective is the cannon and that takes a longer time to be ready again since they want to make it a scarce support weapon.
-The whole plot is at a breakneck speed compared to the manga or anime and it's not even adapted well for a video game, it just doesn't work, it painful, nothing with emotional impact is impactful in the game, hardly anything even makes sense to a first time viewer and it's just painful.
I seriously don't get how they could cut so many corners and not realize that the game would've been so much better with fewer, more unique enemies, a better -maybe Dark Souls like- combat system, and a stronger more drawn out story, it would have been less work to just cut the movies up completely to act as the cutscenes instead of just switching between a butchered movie cut and the lifeless trash they use for the charecter model dialog. I don't understand how this game can be so bad considering I played the AoT: Wings of Freedom game that this company made and it wasn't flawless but it was actually good. This is just emberassing trash and I can only hope that it is easy to mod this game and someone with talent and passion is working on fixing this mess.

I came into this game expecting some decent puzzles and a funny, engaging story. I came out of it feeling I was given neither.
The gameplay of Thomas Was Alone felt less like puzzles and more like walking to the park, except to get to the park you had to stack shapes in obvious ways to clear jumps. There were only a couple of levels that legit felt like they took thinking to complete. All the others challenged my patience more than my processing skills. As well, there were at least three levels where a shape/character ended up in a spot they couldn't jump or die from, meaning I had to manually reset the entire level in order to continue. I also felt the placement of checkpoints in most levels was not consistent; I would receive a checkpoint after completing two long and difficult parts, but then have to complete a simple part and be given yet another checkpoint. Lastly, there were several instances were the game would have too many objects on screen and would drop frames, making some segments more difficult than otherwise.
However, with the overal gameplay, I did feel the game had the potential to use the interesting tools it gave players, it just never did.
The story of Thomas Was Alone starts out interesting when you know little. But once it starts to explain itself, it falls apart and becomes uninteresting. The worst part in the entire story had to be when Thomas  goes to
. When he comes back, the narrator says something along the lines of "Thomas saw cats that couldn't spell right, arrows to the knee, and something about a cake? And a lie?" When this moment happened, I immediately lost all faith in the story. I also cringed pretty hard.
The characters themselves were alright. While they were pretty flat for the most part (development-wise), they had a lot of personality for shapes in a 2D plane. However, I might have prefered if there was no narrator but rather the shapes all had unique voices, and they talked to each other based on different actions or levels.
Overall, I would not recommend buying or playing Thomas Was Alone. If it was a flash game, it would be too long. As a purchasable game on steam, it costs too much.

But the game has many flaws. You are supposed to transport a bunch of people accross the wasteland, but it is just, litterally, a number. You begin with 1000, can loose or gain some depending of scripted events, and that's it. No interaction, no dialogue, no empathy. A number.
Then the fights are based on an arbitrary rule that you can only move twice a turn, even if you have more soldiers (4 max).
Truth be told, that is the same for the ennemies. They do have a rule called "blitz", though, meaning they can from time to time move 3 times. And not you. You also have to gather ressources on the battlefield to continue your journey. All put in the nutshell, it is a greatly frustrating gameplay. It is compared to chess because you have to "chain-cover" your soldiers with others, but the range of attacks are not either 1 case or a straight line, meaning the fights are often confusing and I forget some dude in the process resulting in immediate death among my ranks.
The early game is really difficult, but after some time you can kill everything with just one dude and a huge shotgun. That very dude was killed in the end by a random sniper that has apparently a chance to one shot everything. We are talking about a basic ennemy here, that slained an elite soldier you have to keep levelling up to be effective.
I like difficult games (for exemple I like Darkest dungeon a lot), and I gave this game many tries, but I just don't have fun while fighting, and I don't feel like the commander of an armored vehicle and its inhabitants.
This is however a nice try and the concept is nice.

The game constantly changes whilst not always for the better.. The game can be frustratingly difficult and you will reach the highest difficulty way too quickly because of that! You start of playing in Practice mode (which rewards nothing, ever!) or you get to play Bedlam mode which is actually the hardest even for rookies or veterans alike. The overall look of the game is quite nice, albeit a bit simplified but it does have it's charm. The grid however should have been made more noticeable in order for you to know where exactly to go, or how far the enemies range would be in order for them to shoot your units etc. (due to that you'll lose too many units as of now "Permadeath", which is a real pain in the @#$!!!) There's also no save option, so when you make a mistake or whatever negative event that happened could be very desastrous, really quick and often if you're not careful enough. No second chances with this game whatsoever, making the threshold even higher to begin with. And i can continue further about what should be changed for this game to be amongst my favorites, and i hope it eventually could be in due time if the Devs listen to what most gamers want (finishing the game for once would be a nice change..) etc. Luckily the Devs seem to care about their fans as much as believing in their game, which is always good to have, so i can support the fact that they'll be giving it their best to improve the game..)
So my verdict (not final) is that, i can not fully recommend this game as of now (it does have plenty of potential to be a good game after some time if the game doesn't get abondoned).. Get it at a -50% off discount at least, and do your research first before even trying to get into the game or you'll be disappointed in the long run for sure..

I'd like to preface this review by saying that music has been something that I've enjoyed my whole life. I've been a saxophonist for most of my life, but I've never taken music super seriously. I picked up Rocksmith 2014 without knowing too much about guitar; except that I wanted to learn it. After 6 monthes of playing this game, I can confidently say that this purchase has been one of the best purchases I've made. Before you buy this game, please note that Rocksmith is more of a tool, than a game. The fun of Rocksmith is not in the game itself, but in the improvement of your playing.
Do keep in mind, that when you purchase this game, you really need to buy THREE things along with the game itself to have the best possible experience:
1. The Real Tone Cable for your PC/MAC, so you can connect your guitar or bass to the game.
2. Any Official DLC for the game that you know you will want to learn.
3. Rocksmith 2014 Special Edition song: Cherub Rock by the Smashing Pumpkins.
(or any single official DLC song, I'll take about it shortly!)
I'd recommend that you purchase some official DLC from the store, because the base songs for Rocksmith while good, may be hard for you to get into at first. Playing some of your favorite songs at first will help you to get motivated so you can learn how the game works. When I first started, I started with the DLCs I bought, and so It made learning the game seem more noob-friendly.
I also mentioned that you should purchase the song "Cherub Rock" by the Smashing Pumpkins, if you own this song, it makes downloading mods for the game so much easier because of how the game is coded. It's possible to have access to mods buy purchasing any single official DLC from the store, but the process associated with this method involves a reoccuring identification change (editing the files) that is much to time consuming for most peope. I'd recommend that you purchase Cherub Rock, as this song allows you to have easy access to a plethora of unofficial mods for this game (which are referred to as CDLC- and you must own Cherub Rock to be able to download CDLC). When I say unofficial mods, what I am really talking about are custom songs. These songs are simply free tracks from your favorite bands. For more information on how this system works, I've included some links at the bottom of the page, as well as a few resources and notes. In order to get the best expeirence out of this game, you really need to own Cherub Rock, as then you can have access to so many other artist's songs that the game doesn't support via official DLC or the base tracks, like Metallica, The Red Hot Chilli Peppers, ZZ Top, The Beatles. Paramore, and so so many more artists.
Rocksmith 2014 is a simple game at its core: you see notes on a screen, you play the notes on your guitar or bass in accordance to the on screen note highway, and you do this all to the music of a song. The deisgn of Rocksmith is just digital tab, but a more exciting and interactive tab. Rocksmith works well, and features warm up minigames, various modes for learning and mastering songs, and a improvisational session mode. It's not a very complex game at all, but it's addictive once you sink your teeth into the music. Rocksmith turned a rather casual relationship I had with music, into a rather serious one. The base songs of the game are good, and offer a nice blend of different musical styles and genres to satisfy everyone. I myself found new genres of music that I had never really liked before, and pleasently surpirsed with my growth as both a player and a listener.
If you're on the fence about Rocksmith, buy the game, it will be worth it.

Rocksmith is a great way to learn to play a real guitar (not a fake plastic one). The game itself is immense with arcade style games that make it fun to do exercises that would normally be boring or off-putting, session mode which lets you freestyle with any number of instruments playing along with you intuitively and the DLC is amazingly well-supported and constantly added to. As you learn songs, it dynamically increases the difficulty and forces you to remember them by taking away the queues as you improve so that eventually you can play without help. I couldn't play guitar before but now have several songs I cn confidently play even without the game. Highly recommended.

My daughter started using this when she was seven years old and get rocksmith on xbox just after it came on the market (actually in time for Christmas in 2013).  She quickly became quite good on it, getting 100%+ in quite  a number of songs.   However we discovered that while it is excellent for what it does it is not everything and is no shortcut for hours of practice.  Ive made a few notes below of my thoughts of the programme.
1.    It always sounds good on rocksmith.    I'm not sure exactly how it works but I think that if you play the right note it will generate exactly the right thing in rocksmith regardless of how well you play it.  You might sound awesome on rocksmith but are still♥♥♥♥♥♥♥playing through an amp without the backing music.
2.   It doesnt teach good techniqure.  Sooner or later you will hit a wall unless your technique is good, and it will be difficult to advance.  My daughter started getting lessons six months or so after starting on rocksmith.  Though by that time she was way ahead of all the other 1st year beginners in her class (so it was a great start), professional guitar tutoring from early on has taught her correct technique.
3.   It's attactive graphics and visual cues are a distraction - musicians should be listening.   In my daughters case I think this was ok for initially learning what notes and chords are being played but made it difficult to properly learn the song unless following it on Rocksmith.  My daughter will now use Rocksmith initially only when learning a new song. But most of her practice is just repetition on the amp to get it sounding good and other times just playing along with the soundtrack in the background.
All in all, I like the Rocksmith.  I think it is great for a beginner to start learning and get in interest in playing rock music.  In my daughters case it has opened the door to her discovering something she can become good at,  and it has led to her performing as lead guitarist in a student rock group -  so good fun too.
So I have written this to recommend this product,  but also to let people know of its limitations.  If it fun as a game then fine.  But if they want to become brilliant guitarists like Hendrix or Page then they should get this but also,  sooner rather than later additional tutoring.

Deathspank is a cute little Diablo style action RPG that is based entirely at poking fun at RPG stereotypes. Every line of dialog, every character name, every weapon description, hell, every damn thing in the game is an attempt at some form of humor and while most of it falls flat on it's♥♥♥♥♥some of it will make you chuckle.
Artistically speaking the game is quite nice looking, the graphics are not great but the art style, where everything and everyone is really just a cardboard cutout, fits nicely with the theme of the game. The voice acting is pretty decent although it's hard to judge that in a game where nobody is supposed to sound serious in the first place.
Gameplay is where the game is truly lacking though. You click on an enemy to attack with weapon A and right click for weapon B. The weapons and armor is a completely linear progression and rarely require any input from you.
All in all, it's a fun little game that you will likely enjoy if you don't expect too much from it.

Some things to understand:
- This game is based off of one of the most brutal manga series of all time. While the story arc the game follows can seem pretty freaky/disturbing at times, it does not hold a candle to the manga. Same goes for the Berserk anime and the Golden Age Arcs I, II, & III. If you are interested in the unabridged, and FAR MORE graphic/violent Berserk storyline, please read the manga.
- The story arc for this game DOES NOT catch up to the current place in the manga, but it does go a good bit beyond the anime's current place.
Okie Dokie... anyway... The game.
Berserk and the Band of the Hawk was developed by the same team that does all of the Dynasty Warriors games. It's very simmilar to the Dynasty warrior series in mechanics and layout. However, because this game is based off of a preexisting series, the levels are more mission oriented and focus less on large scale battles. This can be a weclomed change of pace from the usual DW games, but can also become repetitive as many of the maps (or portions of maps) and generic NPC skins are recycled. People unfamiliar with the series may still enjoy the game, but it likely won't become a favorite unless you enjoy the Beserk storyline.
-The artwork is great, but since art is subjective thats really up to personal preference really.          ?/10
-The audio is great if you don't mind subtitles. Same voice actors from the Anime.              10/10
-With the achievements and tons of unlockables, there is plenty of replayability here.              8/10
(The recycled maps and skins can make it feel a little repetitive though)
-Story is based one of the most intense, gritty, violent, and disturbing sagas ever created.        ∞/10
Overall; as a fan I 100% recommend this game to anyone considering buying it. The Berserk storyline is too good to pass up, especially if you're new to the series.

If you like Animal Crossing you'll probably like this. There'll be many instances where you think "compared to Animal Crossing it falls a bit short here." but all in all it's still a great game and a cheaper alternative to Animal Crossing.
Cons:
- farming is fun for a while & it's a good way to make money but it gets boring fast
- you can't do much with the crops you harvested, except for selling them
- Quests can get boring & repeat itself after a while. Sometimes they are a bit annoying, e.g. when you get the quest to pick up some trash and you picked up all the trash on the island some minutes before. You'd have to wait one day (in real time) until there's new trash.
- still a few bugs here and there, most of them can be ignored but sometimes things like accidentally buying the wrong crops happen
- the catalogue is confusing sometimes (in my opinion)
- you can't put furniture or anything else on a tile where you put something like a poster on the wall
Pros:
- at least 20-40 hours of fun (if not even more) for 15$
- lots of things to do (plant flowers/trees, harvest crops, unlock different parts of the island, decorate, catch bugs/fish, collect shells, repair villagers' houses, do quests...)
- the stock market is fun, although there's not much to it
- you can decorate the whole island
- many different kinds of furniture and decorations
- many different kinds of crops, flowers and trees
- unlock new content through daily login rewards
- get rewards through daily quests
- the devs work constantly to fix bugs and put in new content (I reported a bug and got an answer on the same day, a few days later the bug was fixed!)
- the devs listen to the players and take suggestions seriously
Neutral:
- there is no day/night cycle yet but the devs said they are working on it
- after ~20 hours (maybe even less) you'll have all the fish and bugs (and almost all of the shells) in the museum, so there won't be any new ones to catch unless the devs put in new content

Great Animal-Crossing alternative for PC gamers. Offers similar gameplay mechanics suchs as fishing, farming, shopping, socializing with townspeople, etc. Recieves free DLC and updates on occassions and the developer communicates well regarding upcoming features, fixes and addresses and listens to feedback actively. Most importantly, no microtransaction ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t. It seems worthy of a purchase as the features of the Free to play alternative hidden behind a paywall are NOW available to ALL via the reward system by simply progressing through the game on the Steam (PC) version. Not a cent to pay outside of the game's initial asking price.
However, if I had to point out a negative, I'd say the game suffers to a great bit from repetitive quest system, which is used as a method of introducing and advancing the world for the player (you earn rewards, such as gems, in-game currency, to pay to build, unlock the rest of the island and other cosmetic items - no microtransactions!), despite the fact I think that, in theory, this is a nice system of rewarding the player and ensuring a longer playthrough of the game, the quests themselves are repetitive fetch quests and lack any originality and become somewhat tiresome. I feel these could be renovated with more variety to create a more diverse experience by introducing more varied objectives and a deeper backstory to help aid the quest system and maybe offer more depth to the world and characters, to help make them stand out further and help ease the player through and motivate them to care about completing these objectives for the character instead of doing it for gems (or optionally skipping WITH paying gems).
I definitely think the game could stand to take more notes from Animal Crossing. This is a great game at the moment, but still lacks the depth by comparison and I think needs to add more dynamic to the island and it's characters, such as characters moving out and in to the town, weather system, day/night system, and other dynamic features as it will eventually become stale once you've completed played through enough of the games current content and a few changes here and there might work well enough to hold you on for a bit longer.
Nevertheless, the developer has promised to add more features and fixes to the game and listens to feedback. Maybe this review will even help. Who knows? I am still pleased with the game, despite it's flaws and missing features by comparison to Animal Crossing and hope that in time it grows to become a worthy competitor and offer even more depthful gameplay mechanics.

Surprisingly addictive game where you play a family over multiple generations, trying to stay ahead of death, disease and poverty in the era where civilizations spread out of the Fertile Crescent.
The graphics are in a simple but satisfying "animated boardgame" style, and key "events" in the lives of family members are played out as a series of choices in a narrative. Sometimes the "right" choice leads to bad outcomes, and the "wrong" choice to social advancement ---- just like real life!
The story that builds really puts modern life in perspective. Marrying for love definitely took a backseat to marrying for the resources your prospective partner brought to the relationship in those times. Similarly, literally everything revolved around sacrificing as much as possible for your children; every inch of advancement you could buy them was worth it. And not just one child, but making sure you had a "backup" in case of misfortune. But don't spread yourself too thin! Sure children are free labor, but they are also mouths to feed...
I got around 20 hours of fun with this -- so for me it was definitely worth the Steam Sale price I paid for it.

Since I like boardgames, I thought I was going to like this game, but in the end I was dissapointed. It just lacked immersion, and the mechanics can become reptitive that it ends up becoming a grinding slog.
In this game, you try to advance through the board , which in this game is a wheel, using tokens, which you produce by moving backwards, If the wheel ends up dragging you to the wrong end, your character gets eaten by crocodiles.
No, you dont lose the game when that happens, instead you continue with a child-heir of yours, or if you don't have any, a past sibling.
The problem here is that, it is too much luck based, you don't know what tokens you are going to get, and there is a real good chance that you are going to run out of tokens, which means bye-bye and say hello to the crocodiles. This happens especially if you don't get married early, and the matter of you getting married is again dependent on chance and luck.
And if you don't have children, as I have stated above, you continue with a past sibling of yours, which means you will go back a generation. In my case, I was already in the iron age, but went back to the bronze age.
This made me stop playing, As it really felt that the game was never going to end.
Also, the writing which is supposed to bring depth, story, and immersion is weak and uninspired, and most of the time lacking in context - I'm a doctor? no? then a potter? not really, so what am I really? - Such basic questions, the game often fails to answer.
If you like games like checkers or maybe go. You might like this game, but for those seeking for an immersive saga through the ages, like me, we are better off looking someplace else.

I have so much love for this game and I can't quite put a finger on why exactly. It's an endearing mixture of a simple puzzle game that had the option to become frustratingly complicated but wisely decided not to, the writing and narration, and the wonderful soundtrack. People who wish for more complicated challenges need to realise this game isn't about that. It's not the trial and error type thing like INK for example, you're not supposed to border ragequitting.
There were like three or four levels where I struggled and I could've punched my screen listening to the same bit of dialogue every time.
The puzzles serve the story not the other way around which is why if you don't care about the story you won't care for this game.
The writing and narration are stellar to the point where I began to play the rectangles according to their personalities, like the ~meaner ones would go first over a gap, and when given the chance to help another character, it'd always be the ~nicer ones to do so even if more of them had the capability to.
The soundtrack gave the whole game a more epic, more heavy tone that I really appreciated but I understand if it's not everyone's cuppa. For me this game was a wonderful experience and I'll surely be recommending it to others and replaying it. If you accept that this game is story and atmosphere first and difficulty second, you'll have a great time.

You might think this game is so dead-simple it would be impossible to ♥♥♥♥ it up, but the devs found a way to massively hamper the experience anyway. When switching between characters, the order is fixed and may as well be random. The result is that every level with more than 3 characters becomes a total slog. If you want to switch to a specific character, you either have to squint at a tiny bit of UI in the far corner of the screen to figure out what button to press (and how many times to press it), or you have to blindly cycle through until you get to the character you want, which is a painfully slow process for something which should be nearly instantaneous. The obvious solution is to sort characters by their horizontal position on screen - that way, you can switch quickly and without taking your attention away from the level every couple seconds. How the devs didn't think to fix this is absolutely beyond my comprehension.

ADDENDUM 1: 12th of October
Well, there have been some patches since the initial review so I thought it might be a good idea to add my new impressions.
Features: It seems like they try really hard to put, or rather force, in those things they promised. The quality of the implementation seems to reflect the "force" that is used. While there have been several additions to the game, the overall look and feel did not change.
Gameplay: If you can get it to run at more than 6 FPS AND longer than 2 minutes, then the gameplay is still the main challenge. The controls are still wiggly-wobbly as a TARDIS with the handbrake on, but they seem to have improved at least a little bit. I can't play fluently or without a lot of effort but that might just be my personal experience.
Graphics: I use a 8-core Bulldozer CPU and a 4 GB GTX980 with 16GB RAM but even on lowest settings the system struggles to deliver a decent FPS rate while the graphics remind me of Doom. Not the new one, or any sequel, but the first one. The one that came out 1993. So, no improvement on that part.
So they say the final release will be winter 2016? I am praying for this game as I want it to fullfil all the promises it made and become the great game it could actually be, but at the moment, I am still staying true to my original recommendation of "Not recommended".

You ever wanted to travel in a Mad Max like comic apocalypse, through lands filled with Mutants, Marauders, Cyborgs and Rogue Ai enemies, always with the goal to bring as many survivors to the mysterious elysium called Aztec City?
Braving hordes of enemies in tactical combat and always having an eye on your ressources?
Then "Skyshine´s Bedlam" could be interesting for you. The main part is naturally the tactical one, where you can send up to four of your soldiers against the different enemies. This fits to the four basic classes "Deadeyes aka Sharpshooters", "Frontliners aka Meeles", "Trenchers aka Shotgunners" and finally "Gunslingers using Machine Guns".
They mainly are differentiated via their shooting range/damage/health points and mobility.
They can also gain experience for kills, which makes them more useful in general. As there is perma-death for your units, you can quite quickly lose an experienced swat though.
The normal battle takes place on a hexfield with some cover, where you and the enemy can act two times per turn - for your entire squad. This takes some getting used to, but makes it also quite a unique experience in my opinion. On your travels, you can also get some special squad members through choices or battles.
There are quite a bit of choices as you visit different locations, which can for example greatly impact your ressources, which are necessary for getting alive through the wastelands. If you run out of fuel for example, the chances are good that your journey ends in peril.
The story (including profiles for each soldier for example) and soundtrack are atmospheric, while the graphic is fitting, if not quite impressive.
In the long run the motivation for playing is getting higher results as well as unlocking new kind of "Dozers", which are the rolling fortresses in which you move. As with the 2.0 update there are Dozers for each of the factions unlockable, with each having faction-like crews with different abilities. They are also improveable, regarding extra functions and weapons, as well the useage of the ressources.
Conclusio: While Bedlam can have quite unfair moments (especially some of those random events) it offers enough variation and battle possibilities to enjoy quite some playthroughs. Some may have their quarrels with the battle system (which is questionable, even after the last update), but if you get used to it, it can be quite entertaining too, as well as with the balancing.
So... Bedlam surely isn´t for everyone, although i like it.
